Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins﴾ of disbelief, sorcery and other things ﴿that we were the first of the believers﴾ in Musa among these soldiers. So God made them firm and gave them patience. It is possible that Fir'awn did to them what he threatened, by his authority and power at that time; and it is possible that God prevented him from them.

{52} Then Fir'awn and his people remained persistent in their disbelief. Musa came to them with clear signs, and whenever a sign came to them and affected them to the utmost, they promised Musa and covenanted with him that if God removed it from them, they would surely believe in him and surely send the Children of Israel with him. God would remove it, and then they would break their word. When Musa despaired of their belief, the word of punishment was due against them, and it was time for God to rescue the Children of Israel from their captivity and establish them in the land, He inspired Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾; that is, leave with the Children of Israel at the beginning of the night, so that they may proceed and go slowly in their departure. ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾; that is, Fir'awn and his soldiers will follow you. It happened as He had informed: when they awoke, behold, the Children of Israel had all set out with Musa.

{53 – 56} ﴿So Fir'awn sent into the cities gatherers﴾ who gather people, to fall upon the Children of Israel, and he said, encouraging his people: ﴿Indeed, these are a small troop, few in number. And indeed, they are enraging us,﴾ so we intend to vent our rage upon these slaves who have fled from us. ﴿And indeed, we are a vigilant host﴾; that is, we must be on guard against all of them, and they are enemies to all, and the interest is shared.

{57 – 59} So Fir'awn and his soldiers went out in a great army and general mobilization, none remaining behind except those with excuses whom incapacity prevented. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs,﴾ that is, the gardens of Egypt, its excellent orchards, its flowing springs, and crops that filled their lands and populated their cities and countryside with them; ﴿and noble dwellings,﴾ which delight the observers and amaze the contemplators. They enjoyed it for a long age, and they spent a long life in its pleasures and desires, in disbelief, obstinacy, arrogance over the servants, and great bewilderment. ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them,﴾ that is, these gardens, springs, crops and noble dwelling, ﴿the Children of Israel,﴾ whom they had previously made their slaves and subjugated to their hard labor. So glory be to Him who gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips it from whom He wills, exalts whom He wills by obedience to Him, and humbles whom He wills by disobedience to Him.

{60 – 62} ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾; that is, the people of Fir'awn followed the people of Musa at the time of sunrise, driving behind them in anger and rage, capable. ﴿Then when the two companies saw each other﴾; that is, each saw the other. ﴿The companions of Musa said﴾ complaining to Musa and grieved: ﴿Indeed, we are about to be overtaken.﴾ Musa said, making them firm and informing them of the true promise of his Lord: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ to what contains my deliverance and yours.

{63–68} {So We revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff."} So he struck it, {and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain}; that is, like a huge mountain. Moses and his people entered [the path]. {And We brought the others near to that place}; that is, Pharaoh [and] his people. We drew them near and led them into that same path which Moses and his people had taken. {And We delivered Moses and all who were with him}: they completed the crossing, coming out, and not one of them was left behind. {Then We drowned the others}: not one of them was left behind from drowning. {Indeed in that is a sign}: a great sign confirming the truth of what Moses, peace be upon him, brought and the falsehood of what Pharaoh and his people were upon. {Yet most of them were not believers}: despite these signs that call for faith, because of the corruption of your hearts. {And indeed your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful}: by His might He destroyed the disbelieving deniers, and by His mercy He saved Moses and all who were with him.

{10 – 11} Recall the noble state of Musa (Moses) at the time when God called out to him, spoke to him, gave him prophethood and sent him, so He said: ﴿Go to the wrongdoing people,﴾ those who were arrogant upon the earth, exalted themselves over its people, and whose chief claimed lordship; ﴿the people of Fir'awn (Pharaoh). Will they not fear Him?﴾ That is: say to them with gentle speech and tender expression: Will you not fear God, who created you and provided for you, so that you abandon what you are upon of disbelief?

{12 – 14} Musa, peace be upon him, said, making excuse to his Lord, explaining his excuse, and asking Him for help with this heavy burden: ﴿My Lord, I fear that they will deny me. And my breast will be constricted, and my tongue will not be loosened.﴾ So He said: ﴿Expand for me my breast. And ease for me my task. And untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a helper from my family, Harun (Aaron), my brother.﴾ ﴿So send to Harun.﴾ God answered his request and gave prophethood to his brother [Harun] as He had given it to him. ﴿And send him with me as a supporter,﴾ that is, a helper to me in my affair. ﴿And they have a charge against me,﴾ that is, regarding the killing of the Copt, ﴿so I fear that they will kill me.﴾

{15 – 17} ﴿He said: No!﴾ That is: they will not be able to kill you; indeed We will make for you both a sultan (authority), so they will not reach you [by Our signs]. You and those who follow you will be the victorious. This is why Fir'awn was not able to kill Musa, despite his utmost opposition to him, his declaring foolish his opinion, and his misguiding him and his people. ﴿So go, both of you, with Our signs﴾: which indicate your truthfulness and the soundness of what you have brought. ﴿Indeed, We are with you, listening.﴾ I will protect you and watch over you. ﴿So come to Fir'awn and say: Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds;﴾ that is, We have sent to you that you may believe in Him and in Us, submit to His worship, and humble yourself to His monotheism. ﴿That you send with us the Children of Israel.﴾ So withhold from them your punishment, and lift your hand from them, so that they may worship their Lord and establish the affair of their religion.

{18 – 19} When they came to Fir'awn and told him what God had told them, Fir'awn did not believe, did not soften, and began to oppose Musa. So he said: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ That is: Did We not bestow favor upon you and care for your upbringing from when you were a child in your cradle, and you remained so? ﴿And you remained among us for years of your life. And you did your deed which you did﴾: which is the killing of Musa of the Copt when ﴿the one of his own faction called for his help against the one of his enemy, so Musa struck him and killed him...﴾ the verse. ﴿And you are of the disbelievers﴾: that is, you at that time, your way was our way and your path our path in disbelief. Thus he confessed to disbelief on his own account without realizing it.

{20 – 22} Musa said: ﴿I did it then while I was of the astray.﴾ That is: not out of disbelief; it was out of error and foolishness. ﴿So I fled from you when I feared you﴾: when you conspired to kill me. So I fled to Madyan and remained for years; then I came to you, after my Lord had granted me ﴿wisdom and made me of the messengers.﴾

The summary is that Fir'awn's objection to Musa is the objection of an ignorant or feigning person, for he made the obstacle to his being a messenger that a killing had occurred from him. Musa explained to him that his killing was in the manner of error and mistake, not intending the killing itself, and that God's bounty is not withheld from anyone. So why do you prevent what God has bestowed upon me of wisdom and messengership?

There remains, O Fir'awn, your boasting with your saying: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ Upon examination it becomes clear that you have no favor in it. This is why Musa said: ﴿And this is a favor﴾ you recount ﴿upon me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.﴾ That is: you boast to me of this favor because you subjugated the Children of Israel and made them like slaves for you, and you have delivered me from your enslavement and subjugation, and you consider it a favor upon me. Upon reflection it becomes clear that the reality is that you wronged this noble people, tormented them, and subjugated them by your works, while God has protected me from your harm, though your harm reached my people. So what favor is this by which you claim kinship and boast?!

{23 – 25} ﴿Fir'awn said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ This is his denial of his Lord out of injustice and arrogance, despite his certainty of the truth of what Musa called him to. ﴿He said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them;﴾ that is, He who created the upper and lower world, governed it with various kinds of management, and nurtured it with various kinds of nurture, and among that are you, O addressed ones. So how do you deny the Creator of creatures and the Originator of the earth and heavens? ﴿If you are certain.﴾ Then Fir'awn said, mocking and marveling at his words: ﴿Will you not listen?﴾ to what this man says.

{26 – 27} Musa said: ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest.﴾ Whether you marvel or not, whether you are arrogant or submit. Fir'awn said, opposing the truth and disparaging the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad!﴾ For he said what is contrary to what we are upon and opposed us in what we have gone to. So reason, in his view, and the people of reason, are those who claim that they were not created, or that the heavens and earth have always existed without a originator, and that they created themselves without a creator! And reason in his view is that the created deficient in every respect be worshipped! And madness in his view is that the Lord, the Creator of the upper and lower world and the Bestower of apparent and hidden blessings, be affirmed and called to worship! He made this saying attractive to his people, and they were feeble of mind and light of intellect. ﴿So he made his people light-minded, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiant people.﴾

{28} Musa, peace be upon him, said in reply to Fir'awn's denial and negation of the Lord of the worlds: ﴿Lord of the east and the west and what is between them﴾ of all creatures. ﴿If you were to reason.﴾ For I have given you clarification and explanation that every person with even a little sense can understand. So what is wrong with you that you feign ignorance regarding what I address to you? This also contains an allusion and warning that the madness you accused Musa of is in fact your own affliction; you accused the most pure of creation in intellect and most complete in knowledge [of madness]!, while in reality you are the mad ones, since your minds departed from denying the most evident of existents: the Creator of the earth, the heavens and what is between them. If you deny Him, what then do you affirm? If you are ignorant of Him, what then do you know? If you do not believe in Him and His signs, in what then after God and His signs will you believe?! By God, the madmen who are like beasts are more intelligent than you, and the grazing livestock are better guided than you.

{29 – 33} When the proof overwhelmed Fir'awn and his power and eloquence failed to counter it, ﴿he said﴾ threatening Musa with his authority: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned.﴾ He claimed, may God curse him, that he was keen to mislead Musa and that he should not take any god other than himself; otherwise it had been established that he and those with him were in clear insight regarding their affair. So Musa said to him: ﴿Even if I bring you something clear?﴾ That is, a manifest, evident sign of the truth of what I have brought of extraordinary events. ﴿He said: Then bring it, if you are of the truthful. So he threw his staff, and behold, it was a serpent﴾; that is, a mention of serpents. ﴿Clearly visible﴾: manifest to everyone, neither imagination nor likeness. ﴿And he drew out his hand﴾ from his garment, ﴿and behold, it was white to the observers﴾; that is, it had a great light, without any defect, for whoever looked at it.

{34 – 37} ﴿He﴾ Fir'awn ﴿said to the chiefs around him﴾, opposing the truth and the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer. He wants to drive you out of your land.﴾ He deceived them, knowing the weakness of their minds, that this is of the same kind as what sorcerers bring, since it was established among them that sorcerers produce wonders that people cannot do; and he frightened them that his intention by this sorcery was to reach their expulsion from their homeland, so that they would strive and exert themselves in opposing the one who wanted to drive them out from their children and homes. ﴿So what do you advise﴾ that we do with him? ﴿They said: Delay him and his brother﴾; that is, postpone them; ﴿and send into the cities gatherers,﴾ who gather people, ﴿who will bring you every learned sorcerer.﴾ That is: send into all your cities, which are the seat of knowledge and the mine of sorcery, one who will gather for you every skilled and knowledgeable sorcerer in his sorcery; for a sorcerer is confronted with sorcery of its own kind. This is from God's kindness: that He would show His servants the falsity of what Fir'awn, the ignorant, astray and misleading, had deceived them with, that what Musa brought was sorcery. He arranged that they gathered the people skilled in sorcery, so that the assembly would convene in the presence of a great multitude, the truth would prevail over falsehood, and the people of knowledge and craft would acknowledge the soundness of what Musa brought, and that it is not sorcery.

{38 – 40} Fir'awn acted on their opinion, sending into the cities someone to gather the sorcerers, and he strove and exerted himself in this. ﴿So the sorcerers were gathered for the appointment of a known day﴾ which Musa had promised them, and it was the day of adornment, when they were free from their occupations. ﴿And it was said to the people: Will you assemble?﴾; that is, it was announced to the people generally to gather on that promised day. ﴿That we may follow the sorcerers if they are the victors.﴾ That is, they said to the people: Gather so that you may see the sorcerers' victory over Musa, and that they are skilled in their craft, so we may follow them, honor them, and recognize the excellence of the science of sorcery. Had they been granted success in the truth, they would have said: Perhaps we will follow the one among them who is righteous, and recognize what is correct. Therefore this did not benefit them except to establish the proof against them.

{41 – 42} ﴿So when the sorcerers came﴾ and reached Fir'awn, they said to him: ﴿Indeed, will there be a reward for us if we are the victors?﴾ over Musa. ﴿He said: Yes﴾: you will have a reward and recompense, and you will indeed be among those brought near to me. He promised them the reward and nearness to him, so that their energy would increase and they would bring all their capacity in opposing what Musa brought.

{43 – 45} When they gathered at the appointment, they, Musa, and the people of Egypt, Musa admonished them and reminded them and said: ﴿Woe to you! Do not fabricate against God a lie, lest He destroy you with punishment. Indeed, he fails who fabricates.﴾ They disputed and argued among themselves; then Fir'awn encouraged them and some of them encouraged others. ﴿Musa said to them: Throw what you are going to throw﴾; that is, throw whatever is in your minds to throw, and he did not restrict it to anything over anything, due to his certainty of the falsity of what they had come with in opposing the truth. ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs,﴾ and behold, they were snakes moving swiftly, and they deceived the eyes of the people. ﴿And they said: By the might of Fir'awn, indeed we are the victors.﴾ They sought help by the might of a weak servant, helpless in every respect, except that he had become tyrannical and acquired the appearance of kingship and armies, and that splendor deceived them, and their insight did not penetrate to the reality of the matter; or it was an oath by them by the might of Fir'awn, and the thing sworn to is that they are the victors. ﴿Then Musa threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed﴾: it devoured and took ﴿what they had fabricated.﴾ So it seized all that they had thrown of ropes and staffs, because they were a lie, falsehood and fabrication, and all of that is vanity that cannot stand against the truth nor withstand it.

{46 – 48} When the sorcerers saw this great sign, they were certain by their knowledge that this was not sorcery, but a sign of God and a miracle announcing the truthfulness of Musa and the soundness of what he brought. ﴿So the sorcerers fell down prostrate﴾ to their Lord, ﴿saying: We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.﴾ Falsehood was suppressed in that assembly, its leaders acknowledged its falsity, the truth became clear and manifest, so that the onlookers saw it with their own eyes.

{49 – 51} But Fir'awn refused, except in arrogance, misguidance, persistence in his error and obstinacy. He said to the sorcerers: ﴿You believed in him before I gave you permission?﴾ He marveled and made his people marvel at their boldness toward him and their hastiness in believing without his permission and consultation. ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you sorcery.﴾ This is so, though he is the one who gathered the sorcerers and his chiefs who advised him to gather them from their cities, and they knew that they had not met Musa or seen him before that, and that they had brought from sorcery what bewilders the observers and overwhelms them. Despite that, this saying which they themselves had recognized as false became acceptable to them. It is therefore not to be wondered at that people of such minds do not believe in the clear truth and the dazzling signs, for if Fir'awn had told them that it was contrary to its reality, they would have believed him. Then he threatened the sorcerers, saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides﴾; that is, the right hand and the left foot, as is done to the corrupter on earth, ﴿and I will surely crucify you all,﴾ to disgrace and humiliate you. The sorcerers, when they found the sweetness of faith and tasted its delight, said: ﴿No harm!﴾; that is, we do not care about what you threaten us with. ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we will return. Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins﴾ of disbelief, sorcery and other things ﴿that we were the first of the believers﴾ in Musa among these soldiers. So God made them firm and gave them patience. It is possible that Fir'awn did to them what he threatened, by his authority and power at that time; and it is possible that God prevented him from them.

{52} Then Fir'awn and his people remained persistent in their disbelief. Musa came to them with clear signs, and whenever a sign came to them and affected them to the utmost, they promised Musa and covenanted with him that if God removed it from them, they would surely believe in him and surely send the Children of Israel with him. God would remove it, and then they would break their word. When Musa despaired of their belief, the word of punishment was due against them, and it was time for God to rescue the Children of Israel from their captivity and establish them in the land, He inspired Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾; that is, leave with the Children of Israel at the beginning of the night, so that they may proceed and go slowly in their departure. ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾; that is, Fir'awn and his soldiers will follow you. It happened as He had informed: when they awoke, behold, the Children of Israel had all set out with Musa.

{53 – 56} ﴿So Fir'awn sent into the cities gatherers﴾ who gather people, to fall upon the Children of Israel, and he said, encouraging his people: ﴿Indeed, these are a small troop, few in number. And indeed, they are enraging us,﴾ so we intend to vent our rage upon these slaves who have fled from us. ﴿And indeed, we are a vigilant host﴾; that is, we must be on guard against all of them, and they are enemies to all, and the interest is shared.

{57 – 59} So Fir'awn and his soldiers went out in a great army and general mobilization, none remaining behind except those with excuses whom incapacity prevented. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs,﴾ that is, the gardens of Egypt, its excellent orchards, its flowing springs, and crops that filled their lands and populated their cities and countryside with them; ﴿and noble dwellings,﴾ which delight the observers and amaze the contemplators. They enjoyed it for a long age, and they spent a long life in its pleasures and desires, in disbelief, obstinacy, arrogance over the servants, and great bewilderment. ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them,﴾ that is, these gardens, springs, crops and noble dwelling, ﴿the Children of Israel,﴾ whom they had previously made their slaves and subjugated to their hard labor. So glory be to Him who gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips it from whom He wills, exalts whom He wills by obedience to Him, and humbles whom He wills by disobedience to Him.

{60 – 62} ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾; that is, the people of Fir'awn followed the people of Musa at the time of sunrise, driving behind them in anger and rage, capable. ﴿Then when the two companies saw each other﴾; that is, each saw the other. ﴿The companions of Musa said﴾ complaining to Musa and grieved: ﴿Indeed, we are about to be overtaken.﴾ Musa said, making them firm and informing them of the true promise of his Lord: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ to what contains my deliverance and yours.

{63–68} {So We revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff."} So he struck it, {and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain}; that is, like a huge mountain. Moses and his people entered [the path]. {And We brought the others near to that place}; that is, Pharaoh [and] his people. We drew them near and led them into that same path which Moses and his people had taken. {And We delivered Moses and all who were with him}: they completed the crossing, coming out, and not one of them was left behind. {Then We drowned the others}: not one of them was left behind from drowning. {Indeed in that is a sign}: a great sign confirming the truth of what Moses, peace be upon him, brought and the falsehood of what Pharaoh and his people were upon. {Yet most of them were not believers}: despite these signs that call for faith, because of the corruption of your hearts. {And indeed your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful}: by His might He destroyed the disbelieving deniers, and by His mercy He saved Moses and all who were with him.

{10 – 11} Recall the noble state of Musa (Moses) at the time when God called out to him, spoke to him, gave him prophethood and sent him, so He said: ﴿Go to the wrongdoing people,﴾ those who were arrogant upon the earth, exalted themselves over its people, and whose chief claimed lordship; ﴿the people of Fir'awn (Pharaoh). Will they not fear Him?﴾ That is: say to them with gentle speech and tender expression: Will you not fear God, who created you and provided for you, so that you abandon what you are upon of disbelief?

{12 – 14} Musa, peace be upon him, said, making excuse to his Lord, explaining his excuse, and asking Him for help with this heavy burden: ﴿My Lord, I fear that they will deny me. And my breast will be constricted, and my tongue will not be loosened.﴾ So He said: ﴿Expand for me my breast. And ease for me my task. And untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a helper from my family, Harun (Aaron), my brother.﴾ ﴿So send to Harun.﴾ God answered his request and gave prophethood to his brother [Harun] as He had given it to him. ﴿And send him with me as a supporter,﴾ that is, a helper to me in my affair. ﴿And they have a charge against me,﴾ that is, regarding the killing of the Copt, ﴿so I fear that they will kill me.﴾

{15 – 17} ﴿He said: No!﴾ That is: they will not be able to kill you; indeed We will make for you both a sultan (authority), so they will not reach you [by Our signs]. You and those who follow you will be the victorious. This is why Fir'awn was not able to kill Musa, despite his utmost opposition to him, his declaring foolish his opinion, and his misguiding him and his people. ﴿So go, both of you, with Our signs﴾: which indicate your truthfulness and the soundness of what you have brought. ﴿Indeed, We are with you, listening.﴾ I will protect you and watch over you. ﴿So come to Fir'awn and say: Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds;﴾ that is, We have sent to you that you may believe in Him and in Us, submit to His worship, and humble yourself to His monotheism. ﴿That you send with us the Children of Israel.﴾ So withhold from them your punishment, and lift your hand from them, so that they may worship their Lord and establish the affair of their religion.

{18 – 19} When they came to Fir'awn and told him what God had told them, Fir'awn did not believe, did not soften, and began to oppose Musa. So he said: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ That is: Did We not bestow favor upon you and care for your upbringing from when you were a child in your cradle, and you remained so? ﴿And you remained among us for years of your life. And you did your deed which you did﴾: which is the killing of Musa of the Copt when ﴿the one of his own faction called for his help against the one of his enemy, so Musa struck him and killed him...﴾ the verse. ﴿And you are of the disbelievers﴾: that is, you at that time, your way was our way and your path our path in disbelief. Thus he confessed to disbelief on his own account without realizing it.

{20 – 22} Musa said: ﴿I did it then while I was of the astray.﴾ That is: not out of disbelief; it was out of error and foolishness. ﴿So I fled from you when I feared you﴾: when you conspired to kill me. So I fled to Madyan and remained for years; then I came to you, after my Lord had granted me ﴿wisdom and made me of the messengers.﴾

The summary is that Fir'awn's objection to Musa is the objection of an ignorant or feigning person, for he made the obstacle to his being a messenger that a killing had occurred from him. Musa explained to him that his killing was in the manner of error and mistake, not intending the killing itself, and that God's bounty is not withheld from anyone. So why do you prevent what God has bestowed upon me of wisdom and messengership?

There remains, O Fir'awn, your boasting with your saying: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ Upon examination it becomes clear that you have no favor in it. This is why Musa said: ﴿And this is a favor﴾ you recount ﴿upon me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.﴾ That is: you boast to me of this favor because you subjugated the Children of Israel and made them like slaves for you, and you have delivered me from your enslavement and subjugation, and you consider it a favor upon me. Upon reflection it becomes clear that the reality is that you wronged this noble people, tormented them, and subjugated them by your works, while God has protected me from your harm, though your harm reached my people. So what favor is this by which you claim kinship and boast?!

{23 – 25} ﴿Fir'awn said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ This is his denial of his Lord out of injustice and arrogance, despite his certainty of the truth of what Musa called him to. ﴿He said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them;﴾ that is, He who created the upper and lower world, governed it with various kinds of management, and nurtured it with various kinds of nurture, and among that are you, O addressed ones. So how do you deny the Creator of creatures and the Originator of the earth and heavens? ﴿If you are certain.﴾ Then Fir'awn said, mocking and marveling at his words: ﴿Will you not listen?﴾ to what this man says.

{26 – 27} Musa said: ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest.﴾ Whether you marvel or not, whether you are arrogant or submit. Fir'awn said, opposing the truth and disparaging the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad!﴾ For he said what is contrary to what we are upon and opposed us in what we have gone to. So reason, in his view, and the people of reason, are those who claim that they were not created, or that the heavens and earth have always existed without a originator, and that they created themselves without a creator! And reason in his view is that the created deficient in every respect be worshipped! And madness in his view is that the Lord, the Creator of the upper and lower world and the Bestower of apparent and hidden blessings, be affirmed and called to worship! He made this saying attractive to his people, and they were feeble of mind and light of intellect. ﴿So he made his people light-minded, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiant people.﴾

{28} Musa, peace be upon him, said in reply to Fir'awn's denial and negation of the Lord of the worlds: ﴿Lord of the east and the west and what is between them﴾ of all creatures. ﴿If you were to reason.﴾ For I have given you clarification and explanation that every person with even a little sense can understand. So what is wrong with you that you feign ignorance regarding what I address to you? This also contains an allusion and warning that the madness you accused Musa of is in fact your own affliction; you accused the most pure of creation in intellect and most complete in knowledge [of madness]!, while in reality you are the mad ones, since your minds departed from denying the most evident of existents: the Creator of the earth, the heavens and what is between them. If you deny Him, what then do you affirm? If you are ignorant of Him, what then do you know? If you do not believe in Him and His signs, in what then after God and His signs will you believe?! By God, the madmen who are like beasts are more intelligent than you, and the grazing livestock are better guided than you.

{29 – 33} When the proof overwhelmed Fir'awn and his power and eloquence failed to counter it, ﴿he said﴾ threatening Musa with his authority: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned.﴾ He claimed, may God curse him, that he was keen to mislead Musa and that he should not take any god other than himself; otherwise it had been established that he and those with him were in clear insight regarding their affair. So Musa said to him: ﴿Even if I bring you something clear?﴾ That is, a manifest, evident sign of the truth of what I have brought of extraordinary events. ﴿He said: Then bring it, if you are of the truthful. So he threw his staff, and behold, it was a serpent﴾; that is, a mention of serpents. ﴿Clearly visible﴾: manifest to everyone, neither imagination nor likeness. ﴿And he drew out his hand﴾ from his garment, ﴿and behold, it was white to the observers﴾; that is, it had a great light, without any defect, for whoever looked at it.

{34 – 37} ﴿He﴾ Fir'awn ﴿said to the chiefs around him﴾, opposing the truth and the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer. He wants to drive you out of your land.﴾ He deceived them, knowing the weakness of their minds, that this is of the same kind as what sorcerers bring, since it was established among them that sorcerers produce wonders that people cannot do; and he frightened them that his intention by this sorcery was to reach their expulsion from their homeland, so that they would strive and exert themselves in opposing the one who wanted to drive them out from their children and homes. ﴿So what do you advise﴾ that we do with him? ﴿They said: Delay him and his brother﴾; that is, postpone them; ﴿and send into the cities gatherers,﴾ who gather people, ﴿who will bring you every learned sorcerer.﴾ That is: send into all your cities, which are the seat of knowledge and the mine of sorcery, one who will gather for you every skilled and knowledgeable sorcerer in his sorcery; for a sorcerer is confronted with sorcery of its own kind. This is from God's kindness: that He would show His servants the falsity of what Fir'awn, the ignorant, astray and misleading, had deceived them with, that what Musa brought was sorcery. He arranged that they gathered the people skilled in sorcery, so that the assembly would convene in the presence of a great multitude, the truth would prevail over falsehood, and the people of knowledge and craft would acknowledge the soundness of what Musa brought, and that it is not sorcery.

{38 – 40} Fir'awn acted on their opinion, sending into the cities someone to gather the sorcerers, and he strove and exerted himself in this. ﴿So the sorcerers were gathered for the appointment of a known day﴾ which Musa had promised them, and it was the day of adornment, when they were free from their occupations. ﴿And it was said to the people: Will you assemble?﴾; that is, it was announced to the people generally to gather on that promised day. ﴿That we may follow the sorcerers if they are the victors.﴾ That is, they said to the people: Gather so that you may see the sorcerers' victory over Musa, and that they are skilled in their craft, so we may follow them, honor them, and recognize the excellence of the science of sorcery. Had they been granted success in the truth, they would have said: Perhaps we will follow the one among them who is righteous, and recognize what is correct. Therefore this did not benefit them except to establish the proof against them.

{41 – 42} ﴿So when the sorcerers came﴾ and reached Fir'awn, they said to him: ﴿Indeed, will there be a reward for us if we are the victors?﴾ over Musa. ﴿He said: Yes﴾: you will have a reward and recompense, and you will indeed be among those brought near to me. He promised them the reward and nearness to him, so that their energy would increase and they would bring all their capacity in opposing what Musa brought.

{43 – 45} When they gathered at the appointment, they, Musa, and the people of Egypt, Musa admonished them and reminded them and said: ﴿Woe to you! Do not fabricate against God a lie, lest He destroy you with punishment. Indeed, he fails who fabricates.﴾ They disputed and argued among themselves; then Fir'awn encouraged them and some of them encouraged others. ﴿Musa said to them: Throw what you are going to throw﴾; that is, throw whatever is in your minds to throw, and he did not restrict it to anything over anything, due to his certainty of the falsity of what they had come with in opposing the truth. ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs,﴾ and behold, they were snakes moving swiftly, and they deceived the eyes of the people. ﴿And they said: By the might of Fir'awn, indeed we are the victors.﴾ They sought help by the might of a weak servant, helpless in every respect, except that he had become tyrannical and acquired the appearance of kingship and armies, and that splendor deceived them, and their insight did not penetrate to the reality of the matter; or it was an oath by them by the might of Fir'awn, and the thing sworn to is that they are the victors. ﴿Then Musa threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed﴾: it devoured and took ﴿what they had fabricated.﴾ So it seized all that they had thrown of ropes and staffs, because they were a lie, falsehood and fabrication, and all of that is vanity that cannot stand against the truth nor withstand it.

{46 – 48} When the sorcerers saw this great sign, they were certain by their knowledge that this was not sorcery, but a sign of God and a miracle announcing the truthfulness of Musa and the soundness of what he brought. ﴿So the sorcerers fell down prostrate﴾ to their Lord, ﴿saying: We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.﴾ Falsehood was suppressed in that assembly, its leaders acknowledged its falsity, the truth became clear and manifest, so that the onlookers saw it with their own eyes.

{49 – 51} But Fir'awn refused, except in arrogance, misguidance, persistence in his error and obstinacy. He said to the sorcerers: ﴿You believed in him before I gave you permission?﴾ He marveled and made his people marvel at their boldness toward him and their hastiness in believing without his permission and consultation. ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you sorcery.﴾ This is so, though he is the one who gathered the sorcerers and his chiefs who advised him to gather them from their cities, and they knew that they had not met Musa or seen him before that, and that they had brought from sorcery what bewilders the observers and overwhelms them. Despite that, this saying which they themselves had recognized as false became acceptable to them. It is therefore not to be wondered at that people of such minds do not believe in the clear truth and the dazzling signs, for if Fir'awn had told them that it was contrary to its reality, they would have believed him. Then he threatened the sorcerers, saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides﴾; that is, the right hand and the left foot, as is done to the corrupter on earth, ﴿and I will surely crucify you all,﴾ to disgrace and humiliate you. The sorcerers, when they found the sweetness of faith and tasted its delight, said: ﴿No harm!﴾; that is, we do not care about what you threaten us with. ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we will return. Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins﴾ of disbelief, sorcery and other things ﴿that we were the first of the believers﴾ in Musa among these soldiers. So God made them firm and gave them patience. It is possible that Fir'awn did to them what he threatened, by his authority and power at that time; and it is possible that God prevented him from them.

{52} Then Fir'awn and his people remained persistent in their disbelief. Musa came to them with clear signs, and whenever a sign came to them and affected them to the utmost, they promised Musa and covenanted with him that if God removed it from them, they would surely believe in him and surely send the Children of Israel with him. God would remove it, and then they would break their word. When Musa despaired of their belief, the word of punishment was due against them, and it was time for God to rescue the Children of Israel from their captivity and establish them in the land, He inspired Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾; that is, leave with the Children of Israel at the beginning of the night, so that they may proceed and go slowly in their departure. ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾; that is, Fir'awn and his soldiers will follow you. It happened as He had informed: when they awoke, behold, the Children of Israel had all set out with Musa.

{53 – 56} ﴿So Fir'awn sent into the cities gatherers﴾ who gather people, to fall upon the Children of Israel, and he said, encouraging his people: ﴿Indeed, these are a small troop, few in number. And indeed, they are enraging us,﴾ so we intend to vent our rage upon these slaves who have fled from us. ﴿And indeed, we are a vigilant host﴾; that is, we must be on guard against all of them, and they are enemies to all, and the interest is shared.

{57 – 59} So Fir'awn and his soldiers went out in a great army and general mobilization, none remaining behind except those with excuses whom incapacity prevented. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs,﴾ that is, the gardens of Egypt, its excellent orchards, its flowing springs, and crops that filled their lands and populated their cities and countryside with them; ﴿and noble dwellings,﴾ which delight the observers and amaze the contemplators. They enjoyed it for a long age, and they spent a long life in its pleasures and desires, in disbelief, obstinacy, arrogance over the servants, and great bewilderment. ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them,﴾ that is, these gardens, springs, crops and noble dwelling, ﴿the Children of Israel,﴾ whom they had previously made their slaves and subjugated to their hard labor. So glory be to Him who gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips it from whom He wills, exalts whom He wills by obedience to Him, and humbles whom He wills by disobedience to Him.

{60 – 62} ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾; that is, the people of Fir'awn followed the people of Musa at the time of sunrise, driving behind them in anger and rage, capable. ﴿Then when the two companies saw each other﴾; that is, each saw the other. ﴿The companions of Musa said﴾ complaining to Musa and grieved: ﴿Indeed, we are about to be overtaken.﴾ Musa said, making them firm and informing them of the true promise of his Lord: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ to what contains my deliverance and yours.

{63–68} {So We revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff."} So he struck it, {and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain}; that is, like a huge mountain. Moses and his people entered [the path]. {And We brought the others near to that place}; that is, Pharaoh [and] his people. We drew them near and led them into that same path which Moses and his people had taken. {And We delivered Moses and all who were with him}: they completed the crossing, coming out, and not one of them was left behind. {Then We drowned the others}: not one of them was left behind from drowning. {Indeed in that is a sign}: a great sign confirming the truth of what Moses, peace be upon him, brought and the falsehood of what Pharaoh and his people were upon. {Yet most of them were not believers}: despite these signs that call for faith, because of the corruption of your hearts. {And indeed your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful}: by His might He destroyed the disbelieving deniers, and by His mercy He saved Moses and all who were with him.

{10 – 11} Recall the noble state of Musa (Moses) at the time when God called out to him, spoke to him, gave him prophethood and sent him, so He said: ﴿Go to the wrongdoing people,﴾ those who were arrogant upon the earth, exalted themselves over its people, and whose chief claimed lordship; ﴿the people of Fir'awn (Pharaoh). Will they not fear Him?﴾ That is: say to them with gentle speech and tender expression: Will you not fear God, who created you and provided for you, so that you abandon what you are upon of disbelief?

{12 – 14} Musa, peace be upon him, said, making excuse to his Lord, explaining his excuse, and asking Him for help with this heavy burden: ﴿My Lord, I fear that they will deny me. And my breast will be constricted, and my tongue will not be loosened.﴾ So He said: ﴿Expand for me my breast. And ease for me my task. And untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a helper from my family, Harun (Aaron), my brother.﴾ ﴿So send to Harun.﴾ God answered his request and gave prophethood to his brother [Harun] as He had given it to him. ﴿And send him with me as a supporter,﴾ that is, a helper to me in my affair. ﴿And they have a charge against me,﴾ that is, regarding the killing of the Copt, ﴿so I fear that they will kill me.﴾

{15 – 17} ﴿He said: No!﴾ That is: they will not be able to kill you; indeed We will make for you both a sultan (authority), so they will not reach you [by Our signs]. You and those who follow you will be the victorious. This is why Fir'awn was not able to kill Musa, despite his utmost opposition to him, his declaring foolish his opinion, and his misguiding him and his people. ﴿So go, both of you, with Our signs﴾: which indicate your truthfulness and the soundness of what you have brought. ﴿Indeed, We are with you, listening.﴾ I will protect you and watch over you. ﴿So come to Fir'awn and say: Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds;﴾ that is, We have sent to you that you may believe in Him and in Us, submit to His worship, and humble yourself to His monotheism. ﴿That you send with us the Children of Israel.﴾ So withhold from them your punishment, and lift your hand from them, so that they may worship their Lord and establish the affair of their religion.

{18 – 19} When they came to Fir'awn and told him what God had told them, Fir'awn did not believe, did not soften, and began to oppose Musa. So he said: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ That is: Did We not bestow favor upon you and care for your upbringing from when you were a child in your cradle, and you remained so? ﴿And you remained among us for years of your life. And you did your deed which you did﴾: which is the killing of Musa of the Copt when ﴿the one of his own faction called for his help against the one of his enemy, so Musa struck him and killed him...﴾ the verse. ﴿And you are of the disbelievers﴾: that is, you at that time, your way was our way and your path our path in disbelief. Thus he confessed to disbelief on his own account without realizing it.

{20 – 22} Musa said: ﴿I did it then while I was of the astray.﴾ That is: not out of disbelief; it was out of error and foolishness. ﴿So I fled from you when I feared you﴾: when you conspired to kill me. So I fled to Madyan and remained for years; then I came to you, after my Lord had granted me ﴿wisdom and made me of the messengers.﴾

The summary is that Fir'awn's objection to Musa is the objection of an ignorant or feigning person, for he made the obstacle to his being a messenger that a killing had occurred from him. Musa explained to him that his killing was in the manner of error and mistake, not intending the killing itself, and that God's bounty is not withheld from anyone. So why do you prevent what God has bestowed upon me of wisdom and messengership?

There remains, O Fir'awn, your boasting with your saying: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ Upon examination it becomes clear that you have no favor in it. This is why Musa said: ﴿And this is a favor﴾ you recount ﴿upon me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.﴾ That is: you boast to me of this favor because you subjugated the Children of Israel and made them like slaves for you, and you have delivered me from your enslavement and subjugation, and you consider it a favor upon me. Upon reflection it becomes clear that the reality is that you wronged this noble people, tormented them, and subjugated them by your works, while God has protected me from your harm, though your harm reached my people. So what favor is this by which you claim kinship and boast?!

{23 – 25} ﴿Fir'awn said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ This is his denial of his Lord out of injustice and arrogance, despite his certainty of the truth of what Musa called him to. ﴿He said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them;﴾ that is, He who created the upper and lower world, governed it with various kinds of management, and nurtured it with various kinds of nurture, and among that are you, O addressed ones. So how do you deny the Creator of creatures and the Originator of the earth and heavens? ﴿If you are certain.﴾ Then Fir'awn said, mocking and marveling at his words: ﴿Will you not listen?﴾ to what this man says.

{26 – 27} Musa said: ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest.﴾ Whether you marvel or not, whether you are arrogant or submit. Fir'awn said, opposing the truth and disparaging the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad!﴾ For he said what is contrary to what we are upon and opposed us in what we have gone to. So reason, in his view, and the people of reason, are those who claim that they were not created, or that the heavens and earth have always existed without a originator, and that they created themselves without a creator! And reason in his view is that the created deficient in every respect be worshipped! And madness in his view is that the Lord, the Creator of the upper and lower world and the Bestower of apparent and hidden blessings, be affirmed and called to worship! He made this saying attractive to his people, and they were feeble of mind and light of intellect. ﴿So he made his people light-minded, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiant people.﴾

{28} Musa, peace be upon him, said in reply to Fir'awn's denial and negation of the Lord of the worlds: ﴿Lord of the east and the west and what is between them﴾ of all creatures. ﴿If you were to reason.﴾ For I have given you clarification and explanation that every person with even a little sense can understand. So what is wrong with you that you feign ignorance regarding what I address to you? This also contains an allusion and warning that the madness you accused Musa of is in fact your own affliction; you accused the most pure of creation in intellect and most complete in knowledge [of madness]!, while in reality you are the mad ones, since your minds departed from denying the most evident of existents: the Creator of the earth, the heavens and what is between them. If you deny Him, what then do you affirm? If you are ignorant of Him, what then do you know? If you do not believe in Him and His signs, in what then after God and His signs will you believe?! By God, the madmen who are like beasts are more intelligent than you, and the grazing livestock are better guided than you.

{29 – 33} When the proof overwhelmed Fir'awn and his power and eloquence failed to counter it, ﴿he said﴾ threatening Musa with his authority: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned.﴾ He claimed, may God curse him, that he was keen to mislead Musa and that he should not take any god other than himself; otherwise it had been established that he and those with him were in clear insight regarding their affair. So Musa said to him: ﴿Even if I bring you something clear?﴾ That is, a manifest, evident sign of the truth of what I have brought of extraordinary events. ﴿He said: Then bring it, if you are of the truthful. So he threw his staff, and behold, it was a serpent﴾; that is, a mention of serpents. ﴿Clearly visible﴾: manifest to everyone, neither imagination nor likeness. ﴿And he drew out his hand﴾ from his garment, ﴿and behold, it was white to the observers﴾; that is, it had a great light, without any defect, for whoever looked at it.

{34 – 37} ﴿He﴾ Fir'awn ﴿said to the chiefs around him﴾, opposing the truth and the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer. He wants to drive you out of your land.﴾ He deceived them, knowing the weakness of their minds, that this is of the same kind as what sorcerers bring, since it was established among them that sorcerers produce wonders that people cannot do; and he frightened them that his intention by this sorcery was to reach their expulsion from their homeland, so that they would strive and exert themselves in opposing the one who wanted to drive them out from their children and homes. ﴿So what do you advise﴾ that we do with him? ﴿They said: Delay him and his brother﴾; that is, postpone them; ﴿and send into the cities gatherers,﴾ who gather people, ﴿who will bring you every learned sorcerer.﴾ That is: send into all your cities, which are the seat of knowledge and the mine of sorcery, one who will gather for you every skilled and knowledgeable sorcerer in his sorcery; for a sorcerer is confronted with sorcery of its own kind. This is from God's kindness: that He would show His servants the falsity of what Fir'awn, the ignorant, astray and misleading, had deceived them with, that what Musa brought was sorcery. He arranged that they gathered the people skilled in sorcery, so that the assembly would convene in the presence of a great multitude, the truth would prevail over falsehood, and the people of knowledge and craft would acknowledge the soundness of what Musa brought, and that it is not sorcery.

{38 – 40} Fir'awn acted on their opinion, sending into the cities someone to gather the sorcerers, and he strove and exerted himself in this. ﴿So the sorcerers were gathered for the appointment of a known day﴾ which Musa had promised them, and it was the day of adornment, when they were free from their occupations. ﴿And it was said to the people: Will you assemble?﴾; that is, it was announced to the people generally to gather on that promised day. ﴿That we may follow the sorcerers if they are the victors.﴾ That is, they said to the people: Gather so that you may see the sorcerers' victory over Musa, and that they are skilled in their craft, so we may follow them, honor them, and recognize the excellence of the science of sorcery. Had they been granted success in the truth, they would have said: Perhaps we will follow the one among them who is righteous, and recognize what is correct. Therefore this did not benefit them except to establish the proof against them.

{41 – 42} ﴿So when the sorcerers came﴾ and reached Fir'awn, they said to him: ﴿Indeed, will there be a reward for us if we are the victors?﴾ over Musa. ﴿He said: Yes﴾: you will have a reward and recompense, and you will indeed be among those brought near to me. He promised them the reward and nearness to him, so that their energy would increase and they would bring all their capacity in opposing what Musa brought.

{43 – 45} When they gathered at the appointment, they, Musa, and the people of Egypt, Musa admonished them and reminded them and said: ﴿Woe to you! Do not fabricate against God a lie, lest He destroy you with punishment. Indeed, he fails who fabricates.﴾ They disputed and argued among themselves; then Fir'awn encouraged them and some of them encouraged others. ﴿Musa said to them: Throw what you are going to throw﴾; that is, throw whatever is in your minds to throw, and he did not restrict it to anything over anything, due to his certainty of the falsity of what they had come with in opposing the truth. ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs,﴾ and behold, they were snakes moving swiftly, and they deceived the eyes of the people. ﴿And they said: By the might of Fir'awn, indeed we are the victors.﴾ They sought help by the might of a weak servant, helpless in every respect, except that he had become tyrannical and acquired the appearance of kingship and armies, and that splendor deceived them, and their insight did not penetrate to the reality of the matter; or it was an oath by them by the might of Fir'awn, and the thing sworn to is that they are the victors. ﴿Then Musa threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed﴾: it devoured and took ﴿what they had fabricated.﴾ So it seized all that they had thrown of ropes and staffs, because they were a lie, falsehood and fabrication, and all of that is vanity that cannot stand against the truth nor withstand it.

{46 – 48} When the sorcerers saw this great sign, they were certain by their knowledge that this was not sorcery, but a sign of God and a miracle announcing the truthfulness of Musa and the soundness of what he brought. ﴿So the sorcerers fell down prostrate﴾ to their Lord, ﴿saying: We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.﴾ Falsehood was suppressed in that assembly, its leaders acknowledged its falsity, the truth became clear and manifest, so that the onlookers saw it with their own eyes.

{49 – 51} But Fir'awn refused, except in arrogance, misguidance, persistence in his error and obstinacy. He said to the sorcerers: ﴿You believed in him before I gave you permission?﴾ He marveled and made his people marvel at their boldness toward him and their hastiness in believing without his permission and consultation. ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you sorcery.﴾ This is so, though he is the one who gathered the sorcerers and his chiefs who advised him to gather them from their cities, and they knew that they had not met Musa or seen him before that, and that they had brought from sorcery what bewilders the observers and overwhelms them. Despite that, this saying which they themselves had recognized as false became acceptable to them. It is therefore not to be wondered at that people of such minds do not believe in the clear truth and the dazzling signs, for if Fir'awn had told them that it was contrary to its reality, they would have believed him. Then he threatened the sorcerers, saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides﴾; that is, the right hand and the left foot, as is done to the corrupter on earth, ﴿and I will surely crucify you all,﴾ to disgrace and humiliate you. The sorcerers, when they found the sweetness of faith and tasted its delight, said: ﴿No harm!﴾; that is, we do not care about what you threaten us with. ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we will return. Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins﴾ of disbelief, sorcery and other things ﴿that we were the first of the believers﴾ in Musa among these soldiers. So God made them firm and gave them patience. It is possible that Fir'awn did to them what he threatened, by his authority and power at that time; and it is possible that God prevented him from them.

{52} Then Fir'awn and his people remained persistent in their disbelief. Musa came to them with clear signs, and whenever a sign came to them and affected them to the utmost, they promised Musa and covenanted with him that if God removed it from them, they would surely believe in him and surely send the Children of Israel with him. God would remove it, and then they would break their word. When Musa despaired of their belief, the word of punishment was due against them, and it was time for God to rescue the Children of Israel from their captivity and establish them in the land, He inspired Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾; that is, leave with the Children of Israel at the beginning of the night, so that they may proceed and go slowly in their departure. ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾; that is, Fir'awn and his soldiers will follow you. It happened as He had informed: when they awoke, behold, the Children of Israel had all set out with Musa.

{53 – 56} ﴿So Fir'awn sent into the cities gatherers﴾ who gather people, to fall upon the Children of Israel, and he said, encouraging his people: ﴿Indeed, these are a small troop, few in number. And indeed, they are enraging us,﴾ so we intend to vent our rage upon these slaves who have fled from us. ﴿And indeed, we are a vigilant host﴾; that is, we must be on guard against all of them, and they are enemies to all, and the interest is shared.

{57 – 59} So Fir'awn and his soldiers went out in a great army and general mobilization, none remaining behind except those with excuses whom incapacity prevented. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs,﴾ that is, the gardens of Egypt, its excellent orchards, its flowing springs, and crops that filled their lands and populated their cities and countryside with them; ﴿and noble dwellings,﴾ which delight the observers and amaze the contemplators. They enjoyed it for a long age, and they spent a long life in its pleasures and desires, in disbelief, obstinacy, arrogance over the servants, and great bewilderment. ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them,﴾ that is, these gardens, springs, crops and noble dwelling, ﴿the Children of Israel,﴾ whom they had previously made their slaves and subjugated to their hard labor. So glory be to Him who gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips it from whom He wills, exalts whom He wills by obedience to Him, and humbles whom He wills by disobedience to Him.

{60 – 62} ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾; that is, the people of Fir'awn followed the people of Musa at the time of sunrise, driving behind them in anger and rage, capable. ﴿Then when the two companies saw each other﴾; that is, each saw the other. ﴿The companions of Musa said﴾ complaining to Musa and grieved: ﴿Indeed, we are about to be overtaken.﴾ Musa said, making them firm and informing them of the true promise of his Lord: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ to what contains my deliverance and yours.

{63–68} {So We revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff."} So he struck it, {and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain}; that is, like a huge mountain. Moses and his people entered [the path]. {And We brought the others near to that place}; that is, Pharaoh [and] his people. We drew them near and led them into that same path which Moses and his people had taken. {And We delivered Moses and all who were with him}: they completed the crossing, coming out, and not one of them was left behind. {Then We drowned the others}: not one of them was left behind from drowning. {Indeed in that is a sign}: a great sign confirming the truth of what Moses, peace be upon him, brought and the falsehood of what Pharaoh and his people were upon. {Yet most of them were not believers}: despite these signs that call for faith, because of the corruption of your hearts. {And indeed your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful}: by His might He destroyed the disbelieving deniers, and by His mercy He saved Moses and all who were with him.

{10 – 11} Recall the noble state of Musa (Moses) at the time when God called out to him, spoke to him, gave him prophethood and sent him, so He said: ﴿Go to the wrongdoing people,﴾ those who were arrogant upon the earth, exalted themselves over its people, and whose chief claimed lordship; ﴿the people of Fir'awn (Pharaoh). Will they not fear Him?﴾ That is: say to them with gentle speech and tender expression: Will you not fear God, who created you and provided for you, so that you abandon what you are upon of disbelief?

{12 – 14} Musa, peace be upon him, said, making excuse to his Lord, explaining his excuse, and asking Him for help with this heavy burden: ﴿My Lord, I fear that they will deny me. And my breast will be constricted, and my tongue will not be loosened.﴾ So He said: ﴿Expand for me my breast. And ease for me my task. And untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a helper from my family, Harun (Aaron), my brother.﴾ ﴿So send to Harun.﴾ God answered his request and gave prophethood to his brother [Harun] as He had given it to him. ﴿And send him with me as a supporter,﴾ that is, a helper to me in my affair. ﴿And they have a charge against me,﴾ that is, regarding the killing of the Copt, ﴿so I fear that they will kill me.﴾

{15 – 17} ﴿He said: No!﴾ That is: they will not be able to kill you; indeed We will make for you both a sultan (authority), so they will not reach you [by Our signs]. You and those who follow you will be the victorious. This is why Fir'awn was not able to kill Musa, despite his utmost opposition to him, his declaring foolish his opinion, and his misguiding him and his people. ﴿So go, both of you, with Our signs﴾: which indicate your truthfulness and the soundness of what you have brought. ﴿Indeed, We are with you, listening.﴾ I will protect you and watch over you. ﴿So come to Fir'awn and say: Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds;﴾ that is, We have sent to you that you may believe in Him and in Us, submit to His worship, and humble yourself to His monotheism. ﴿That you send with us the Children of Israel.﴾ So withhold from them your punishment, and lift your hand from them, so that they may worship their Lord and establish the affair of their religion.

{18 – 19} When they came to Fir'awn and told him what God had told them, Fir'awn did not believe, did not soften, and began to oppose Musa. So he said: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ That is: Did We not bestow favor upon you and care for your upbringing from when you were a child in your cradle, and you remained so? ﴿And you remained among us for years of your life. And you did your deed which you did﴾: which is the killing of Musa of the Copt when ﴿the one of his own faction called for his help against the one of his enemy, so Musa struck him and killed him...﴾ the verse. ﴿And you are of the disbelievers﴾: that is, you at that time, your way was our way and your path our path in disbelief. Thus he confessed to disbelief on his own account without realizing it.

{20 – 22} Musa said: ﴿I did it then while I was of the astray.﴾ That is: not out of disbelief; it was out of error and foolishness. ﴿So I fled from you when I feared you﴾: when you conspired to kill me. So I fled to Madyan and remained for years; then I came to you, after my Lord had granted me ﴿wisdom and made me of the messengers.﴾

The summary is that Fir'awn's objection to Musa is the objection of an ignorant or feigning person, for he made the obstacle to his being a messenger that a killing had occurred from him. Musa explained to him that his killing was in the manner of error and mistake, not intending the killing itself, and that God's bounty is not withheld from anyone. So why do you prevent what God has bestowed upon me of wisdom and messengership?

There remains, O Fir'awn, your boasting with your saying: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ Upon examination it becomes clear that you have no favor in it. This is why Musa said: ﴿And this is a favor﴾ you recount ﴿upon me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.﴾ That is: you boast to me of this favor because you subjugated the Children of Israel and made them like slaves for you, and you have delivered me from your enslavement and subjugation, and you consider it a favor upon me. Upon reflection it becomes clear that the reality is that you wronged this noble people, tormented them, and subjugated them by your works, while God has protected me from your harm, though your harm reached my people. So what favor is this by which you claim kinship and boast?!

{23 – 25} ﴿Fir'awn said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ This is his denial of his Lord out of injustice and arrogance, despite his certainty of the truth of what Musa called him to. ﴿He said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them;﴾ that is, He who created the upper and lower world, governed it with various kinds of management, and nurtured it with various kinds of nurture, and among that are you, O addressed ones. So how do you deny the Creator of creatures and the Originator of the earth and heavens? ﴿If you are certain.﴾ Then Fir'awn said, mocking and marveling at his words: ﴿Will you not listen?﴾ to what this man says.

{26 – 27} Musa said: ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest.﴾ Whether you marvel or not, whether you are arrogant or submit. Fir'awn said, opposing the truth and disparaging the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad!﴾ For he said what is contrary to what we are upon and opposed us in what we have gone to. So reason, in his view, and the people of reason, are those who claim that they were not created, or that the heavens and earth have always existed without a originator, and that they created themselves without a creator! And reason in his view is that the created deficient in every respect be worshipped! And madness in his view is that the Lord, the Creator of the upper and lower world and the Bestower of apparent and hidden blessings, be affirmed and called to worship! He made this saying attractive to his people, and they were feeble of mind and light of intellect. ﴿So he made his people light-minded, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiant people.﴾

{28} Musa, peace be upon him, said in reply to Fir'awn's denial and negation of the Lord of the worlds: ﴿Lord of the east and the west and what is between them﴾ of all creatures. ﴿If you were to reason.﴾ For I have given you clarification and explanation that every person with even a little sense can understand. So what is wrong with you that you feign ignorance regarding what I address to you? This also contains an allusion and warning that the madness you accused Musa of is in fact your own affliction; you accused the most pure of creation in intellect and most complete in knowledge [of madness]!, while in reality you are the mad ones, since your minds departed from denying the most evident of existents: the Creator of the earth, the heavens and what is between them. If you deny Him, what then do you affirm? If you are ignorant of Him, what then do you know? If you do not believe in Him and His signs, in what then after God and His signs will you believe?! By God, the madmen who are like beasts are more intelligent than you, and the grazing livestock are better guided than you.

{29 – 33} When the proof overwhelmed Fir'awn and his power and eloquence failed to counter it, ﴿he said﴾ threatening Musa with his authority: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned.﴾ He claimed, may God curse him, that he was keen to mislead Musa and that he should not take any god other than himself; otherwise it had been established that he and those with him were in clear insight regarding their affair. So Musa said to him: ﴿Even if I bring you something clear?﴾ That is, a manifest, evident sign of the truth of what I have brought of extraordinary events. ﴿He said: Then bring it, if you are of the truthful. So he threw his staff, and behold, it was a serpent﴾; that is, a mention of serpents. ﴿Clearly visible﴾: manifest to everyone, neither imagination nor likeness. ﴿And he drew out his hand﴾ from his garment, ﴿and behold, it was white to the observers﴾; that is, it had a great light, without any defect, for whoever looked at it.

{34 – 37} ﴿He﴾ Fir'awn ﴿said to the chiefs around him﴾, opposing the truth and the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer. He wants to drive you out of your land.﴾ He deceived them, knowing the weakness of their minds, that this is of the same kind as what sorcerers bring, since it was established among them that sorcerers produce wonders that people cannot do; and he frightened them that his intention by this sorcery was to reach their expulsion from their homeland, so that they would strive and exert themselves in opposing the one who wanted to drive them out from their children and homes. ﴿So what do you advise﴾ that we do with him? ﴿They said: Delay him and his brother﴾; that is, postpone them; ﴿and send into the cities gatherers,﴾ who gather people, ﴿who will bring you every learned sorcerer.﴾ That is: send into all your cities, which are the seat of knowledge and the mine of sorcery, one who will gather for you every skilled and knowledgeable sorcerer in his sorcery; for a sorcerer is confronted with sorcery of its own kind. This is from God's kindness: that He would show His servants the falsity of what Fir'awn, the ignorant, astray and misleading, had deceived them with, that what Musa brought was sorcery. He arranged that they gathered the people skilled in sorcery, so that the assembly would convene in the presence of a great multitude, the truth would prevail over falsehood, and the people of knowledge and craft would acknowledge the soundness of what Musa brought, and that it is not sorcery.

{38 – 40} Fir'awn acted on their opinion, sending into the cities someone to gather the sorcerers, and he strove and exerted himself in this. ﴿So the sorcerers were gathered for the appointment of a known day﴾ which Musa had promised them, and it was the day of adornment, when they were free from their occupations. ﴿And it was said to the people: Will you assemble?﴾; that is, it was announced to the people generally to gather on that promised day. ﴿That we may follow the sorcerers if they are the victors.﴾ That is, they said to the people: Gather so that you may see the sorcerers' victory over Musa, and that they are skilled in their craft, so we may follow them, honor them, and recognize the excellence of the science of sorcery. Had they been granted success in the truth, they would have said: Perhaps we will follow the one among them who is righteous, and recognize what is correct. Therefore this did not benefit them except to establish the proof against them.

{41 – 42} ﴿So when the sorcerers came﴾ and reached Fir'awn, they said to him: ﴿Indeed, will there be a reward for us if we are the victors?﴾ over Musa. ﴿He said: Yes﴾: you will have a reward and recompense, and you will indeed be among those brought near to me. He promised them the reward and nearness to him, so that their energy would increase and they would bring all their capacity in opposing what Musa brought.

{43 – 45} When they gathered at the appointment, they, Musa, and the people of Egypt, Musa admonished them and reminded them and said: ﴿Woe to you! Do not fabricate against God a lie, lest He destroy you with punishment. Indeed, he fails who fabricates.﴾ They disputed and argued among themselves; then Fir'awn encouraged them and some of them encouraged others. ﴿Musa said to them: Throw what you are going to throw﴾; that is, throw whatever is in your minds to throw, and he did not restrict it to anything over anything, due to his certainty of the falsity of what they had come with in opposing the truth. ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs,﴾ and behold, they were snakes moving swiftly, and they deceived the eyes of the people. ﴿And they said: By the might of Fir'awn, indeed we are the victors.﴾ They sought help by the might of a weak servant, helpless in every respect, except that he had become tyrannical and acquired the appearance of kingship and armies, and that splendor deceived them, and their insight did not penetrate to the reality of the matter; or it was an oath by them by the might of Fir'awn, and the thing sworn to is that they are the victors. ﴿Then Musa threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed﴾: it devoured and took ﴿what they had fabricated.﴾ So it seized all that they had thrown of ropes and staffs, because they were a lie, falsehood and fabrication, and all of that is vanity that cannot stand against the truth nor withstand it.

{46 – 48} When the sorcerers saw this great sign, they were certain by their knowledge that this was not sorcery, but a sign of God and a miracle announcing the truthfulness of Musa and the soundness of what he brought. ﴿So the sorcerers fell down prostrate﴾ to their Lord, ﴿saying: We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.﴾ Falsehood was suppressed in that assembly, its leaders acknowledged its falsity, the truth became clear and manifest, so that the onlookers saw it with their own eyes.

{49 – 51} But Fir'awn refused, except in arrogance, misguidance, persistence in his error and obstinacy. He said to the sorcerers: ﴿You believed in him before I gave you permission?﴾ He marveled and made his people marvel at their boldness toward him and their hastiness in believing without his permission and consultation. ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you sorcery.﴾ This is so, though he is the one who gathered the sorcerers and his chiefs who advised him to gather them from their cities, and they knew that they had not met Musa or seen him before that, and that they had brought from sorcery what bewilders the observers and overwhelms them. Despite that, this saying which they themselves had recognized as false became acceptable to them. It is therefore not to be wondered at that people of such minds do not believe in the clear truth and the dazzling signs, for if Fir'awn had told them that it was contrary to its reality, they would have believed him. Then he threatened the sorcerers, saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides﴾; that is, the right hand and the left foot, as is done to the corrupter on earth, ﴿and I will surely crucify you all,﴾ to disgrace and humiliate you. The sorcerers, when they found the sweetness of faith and tasted its delight, said: ﴿No harm!﴾; that is, we do not care about what you threaten us with. ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we will return. Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins﴾ of disbelief, sorcery and other things ﴿that we were the first of the believers﴾ in Musa among these soldiers. So God made them firm and gave them patience. It is possible that Fir'awn did to them what he threatened, by his authority and power at that time; and it is possible that God prevented him from them.

{52} Then Fir'awn and his people remained persistent in their disbelief. Musa came to them with clear signs, and whenever a sign came to them and affected them to the utmost, they promised Musa and covenanted with him that if God removed it from them, they would surely believe in him and surely send the Children of Israel with him. God would remove it, and then they would break their word. When Musa despaired of their belief, the word of punishment was due against them, and it was time for God to rescue the Children of Israel from their captivity and establish them in the land, He inspired Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾; that is, leave with the Children of Israel at the beginning of the night, so that they may proceed and go slowly in their departure. ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾; that is, Fir'awn and his soldiers will follow you. It happened as He had informed: when they awoke, behold, the Children of Israel had all set out with Musa.

{53 – 56} ﴿So Fir'awn sent into the cities gatherers﴾ who gather people, to fall upon the Children of Israel, and he said, encouraging his people: ﴿Indeed, these are a small troop, few in number. And indeed, they are enraging us,﴾ so we intend to vent our rage upon these slaves who have fled from us. ﴿And indeed, we are a vigilant host﴾; that is, we must be on guard against all of them, and they are enemies to all, and the interest is shared.

{57 – 59} So Fir'awn and his soldiers went out in a great army and general mobilization, none remaining behind except those with excuses whom incapacity prevented. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs,﴾ that is, the gardens of Egypt, its excellent orchards, its flowing springs, and crops that filled their lands and populated their cities and countryside with them; ﴿and noble dwellings,﴾ which delight the observers and amaze the contemplators. They enjoyed it for a long age, and they spent a long life in its pleasures and desires, in disbelief, obstinacy, arrogance over the servants, and great bewilderment. ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them,﴾ that is, these gardens, springs, crops and noble dwelling, ﴿the Children of Israel,﴾ whom they had previously made their slaves and subjugated to their hard labor. So glory be to Him who gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips it from whom He wills, exalts whom He wills by obedience to Him, and humbles whom He wills by disobedience to Him.
