They enjoyed it for a long age, and they spent a long life in its pleasures and desires, in disbelief, obstinacy, arrogance over the servants, and great bewilderment. ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them,﴾ that is, these gardens, springs, crops and noble dwelling, ﴿the Children of Israel,﴾ whom they had previously made their slaves and subjugated to their hard labor. So glory be to Him who gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips it from whom He wills, exalts whom He wills by obedience to Him, and humbles whom He wills by disobedience to Him.

{60 – 62} ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾; that is, the people of Fir'awn followed the people of Musa at the time of sunrise, driving behind them in anger and rage, capable. ﴿Then when the two companies saw each other﴾; that is, each saw the other. ﴿The companions of Musa said﴾ complaining to Musa and grieved: ﴿Indeed, we are about to be overtaken.﴾ Musa said, making them firm and informing them of the true promise of his Lord: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ to what contains my deliverance and yours.

{63–68} {So We revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff."} So he struck it, {and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain}; that is, like a huge mountain. Moses and his people entered [the path]. {And We brought the others near to that place}; that is, Pharaoh [and] his people. We drew them near and led them into that same path which Moses and his people had taken. {And We delivered Moses and all who were with him}: they completed the crossing, coming out, and not one of them was left behind. {Then We drowned the others}: not one of them was left behind from drowning. {Indeed in that is a sign}: a great sign confirming the truth of what Moses, peace be upon him, brought and the falsehood of what Pharaoh and his people were upon. {Yet most of them were not believers}: despite these signs that call for faith, because of the corruption of your hearts. {And indeed your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful}: by His might He destroyed the disbelieving deniers, and by His mercy He saved Moses and all who were with him.

{10 – 11} Recall the noble state of Musa (Moses) at the time when God called out to him, spoke to him, gave him prophethood and sent him, so He said: ﴿Go to the wrongdoing people,﴾ those who were arrogant upon the earth, exalted themselves over its people, and whose chief claimed lordship; ﴿the people of Fir'awn (Pharaoh). Will they not fear Him?﴾ That is: say to them with gentle speech and tender expression: Will you not fear God, who created you and provided for you, so that you abandon what you are upon of disbelief?

{12 – 14} Musa, peace be upon him, said, making excuse to his Lord, explaining his excuse, and asking Him for help with this heavy burden: ﴿My Lord, I fear that they will deny me. And my breast will be constricted, and my tongue will not be loosened.﴾ So He said: ﴿Expand for me my breast. And ease for me my task. And untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a helper from my family, Harun (Aaron), my brother.﴾ ﴿So send to Harun.﴾ God answered his request and gave prophethood to his brother [Harun] as He had given it to him. ﴿And send him with me as a supporter,﴾ that is, a helper to me in my affair. ﴿And they have a charge against me,﴾ that is, regarding the killing of the Copt, ﴿so I fear that they will kill me.﴾

{15 – 17} ﴿He said: No!﴾ That is: they will not be able to kill you; indeed We will make for you both a sultan (authority), so they will not reach you [by Our signs]. You and those who follow you will be the victorious. This is why Fir'awn was not able to kill Musa, despite his utmost opposition to him, his declaring foolish his opinion, and his misguiding him and his people. ﴿So go, both of you, with Our signs﴾: which indicate your truthfulness and the soundness of what you have brought. ﴿Indeed, We are with you, listening.﴾ I will protect you and watch over you. ﴿So come to Fir'awn and say: Indeed, we are messengers of the Lord of the worlds;﴾ that is, We have sent to you that you may believe in Him and in Us, submit to His worship, and humble yourself to His monotheism. ﴿That you send with us the Children of Israel.﴾ So withhold from them your punishment, and lift your hand from them, so that they may worship their Lord and establish the affair of their religion.

{18 – 19} When they came to Fir'awn and told him what God had told them, Fir'awn did not believe, did not soften, and began to oppose Musa. So he said: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ That is: Did We not bestow favor upon you and care for your upbringing from when you were a child in your cradle, and you remained so? ﴿And you remained among us for years of your life. And you did your deed which you did﴾: which is the killing of Musa of the Copt when ﴿the one of his own faction called for his help against the one of his enemy, so Musa struck him and killed him...﴾ the verse. ﴿And you are of the disbelievers﴾: that is, you at that time, your way was our way and your path our path in disbelief. Thus he confessed to disbelief on his own account without realizing it.

{20 – 22} Musa said: ﴿I did it then while I was of the astray.﴾ That is: not out of disbelief; it was out of error and foolishness. ﴿So I fled from you when I feared you﴾: when you conspired to kill me. So I fled to Madyan and remained for years; then I came to you, after my Lord had granted me ﴿wisdom and made me of the messengers.﴾

The summary is that Fir'awn's objection to Musa is the objection of an ignorant or feigning person, for he made the obstacle to his being a messenger that a killing had occurred from him. Musa explained to him that his killing was in the manner of error and mistake, not intending the killing itself, and that God's bounty is not withheld from anyone. So why do you prevent what God has bestowed upon me of wisdom and messengership?

There remains, O Fir'awn, your boasting with your saying: ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child?﴾ Upon examination it becomes clear that you have no favor in it. This is why Musa said: ﴿And this is a favor﴾ you recount ﴿upon me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel.﴾ That is: you boast to me of this favor because you subjugated the Children of Israel and made them like slaves for you, and you have delivered me from your enslavement and subjugation, and you consider it a favor upon me. Upon reflection it becomes clear that the reality is that you wronged this noble people, tormented them, and subjugated them by your works, while God has protected me from your harm, though your harm reached my people. So what favor is this by which you claim kinship and boast?!

{23 – 25} ﴿Fir'awn said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ This is his denial of his Lord out of injustice and arrogance, despite his certainty of the truth of what Musa called him to. ﴿He said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them;﴾ that is, He who created the upper and lower world, governed it with various kinds of management, and nurtured it with various kinds of nurture, and among that are you, O addressed ones. So how do you deny the Creator of creatures and the Originator of the earth and heavens? ﴿If you are certain.﴾ Then Fir'awn said, mocking and marveling at his words: ﴿Will you not listen?﴾ to what this man says.

{26 – 27} Musa said: ﴿Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, the earliest.﴾ Whether you marvel or not, whether you are arrogant or submit. Fir'awn said, opposing the truth and disparaging the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad!﴾ For he said what is contrary to what we are upon and opposed us in what we have gone to. So reason, in his view, and the people of reason, are those who claim that they were not created, or that the heavens and earth have always existed without a originator, and that they created themselves without a creator! And reason in his view is that the created deficient in every respect be worshipped! And madness in his view is that the Lord, the Creator of the upper and lower world and the Bestower of apparent and hidden blessings, be affirmed and called to worship! He made this saying attractive to his people, and they were feeble of mind and light of intellect. ﴿So he made his people light-minded, and they obeyed him. Indeed, they were a defiant people.﴾

{28} Musa, peace be upon him, said in reply to Fir'awn's denial and negation of the Lord of the worlds: ﴿Lord of the east and the west and what is between them﴾ of all creatures. ﴿If you were to reason.﴾ For I have given you clarification and explanation that every person with even a little sense can understand. So what is wrong with you that you feign ignorance regarding what I address to you? This also contains an allusion and warning that the madness you accused Musa of is in fact your own affliction; you accused the most pure of creation in intellect and most complete in knowledge [of madness]!, while in reality you are the mad ones, since your minds departed from denying the most evident of existents: the Creator of the earth, the heavens and what is between them. If you deny Him, what then do you affirm? If you are ignorant of Him, what then do you know? If you do not believe in Him and His signs, in what then after God and His signs will you believe?! By God, the madmen who are like beasts are more intelligent than you, and the grazing livestock are better guided than you.

{29 – 33} When the proof overwhelmed Fir'awn and his power and eloquence failed to counter it, ﴿he said﴾ threatening Musa with his authority: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned.﴾ He claimed, may God curse him, that he was keen to mislead Musa and that he should not take any god other than himself; otherwise it had been established that he and those with him were in clear insight regarding their affair. So Musa said to him: ﴿Even if I bring you something clear?﴾ That is, a manifest, evident sign of the truth of what I have brought of extraordinary events. ﴿He said: Then bring it, if you are of the truthful. So he threw his staff, and behold, it was a serpent﴾; that is, a mention of serpents. ﴿Clearly visible﴾: manifest to everyone, neither imagination nor likeness. ﴿And he drew out his hand﴾ from his garment, ﴿and behold, it was white to the observers﴾; that is, it had a great light, without any defect, for whoever looked at it.

{34 – 37} ﴿He﴾ Fir'awn ﴿said to the chiefs around him﴾, opposing the truth and the one who brought it: ﴿Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer. He wants to drive you out of your land.﴾ He deceived them, knowing the weakness of their minds, that this is of the same kind as what sorcerers bring, since it was established among them that sorcerers produce wonders that people cannot do; and he frightened them that his intention by this sorcery was to reach their expulsion from their homeland, so that they would strive and exert themselves in opposing the one who wanted to drive them out from their children and homes. ﴿So what do you advise﴾ that we do with him? ﴿They said: Delay him and his brother﴾; that is, postpone them; ﴿and send into the cities gatherers,﴾ who gather people, ﴿who will bring you every learned sorcerer.﴾ That is: send into all your cities, which are the seat of knowledge and the mine of sorcery, one who will gather for you every skilled and knowledgeable sorcerer in his sorcery; for a sorcerer is confronted with sorcery of its own kind. This is from God's kindness: that He would show His servants the falsity of what Fir'awn, the ignorant, astray and misleading, had deceived them with, that what Musa brought was sorcery. He arranged that they gathered the people skilled in sorcery, so that the assembly would convene in the presence of a great multitude, the truth would prevail over falsehood, and the people of knowledge and craft would acknowledge the soundness of what Musa brought, and that it is not sorcery.

{38 – 40} Fir'awn acted on their opinion, sending into the cities someone to gather the sorcerers, and he strove and exerted himself in this. ﴿So the sorcerers were gathered for the appointment of a known day﴾ which Musa had promised them, and it was the day of adornment, when they were free from their occupations. ﴿And it was said to the people: Will you assemble?﴾; that is, it was announced to the people generally to gather on that promised day. ﴿That we may follow the sorcerers if they are the victors.﴾ That is, they said to the people: Gather so that you may see the sorcerers' victory over Musa, and that they are skilled in their craft, so we may follow them, honor them, and recognize the excellence of the science of sorcery. Had they been granted success in the truth, they would have said: Perhaps we will follow the one among them who is righteous, and recognize what is correct. Therefore this did not benefit them except to establish the proof against them.

{41 – 42} ﴿So when the sorcerers came﴾ and reached Fir'awn, they said to him: ﴿Indeed, will there be a reward for us if we are the victors?﴾ over Musa. ﴿He said: Yes﴾: you will have a reward and recompense, and you will indeed be among those brought near to me. He promised them the reward and nearness to him, so that their energy would increase and they would bring all their capacity in opposing what Musa brought.

{43 – 45} When they gathered at the appointment, they, Musa, and the people of Egypt, Musa admonished them and reminded them and said: ﴿Woe to you! Do not fabricate against God a lie, lest He destroy you with punishment. Indeed, he fails who fabricates.﴾ They disputed and argued among themselves; then Fir'awn encouraged them and some of them encouraged others. ﴿Musa said to them: Throw what you are going to throw﴾; that is, throw whatever is in your minds to throw, and he did not restrict it to anything over anything, due to his certainty of the falsity of what they had come with in opposing the truth. ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs,﴾ and behold, they were snakes moving swiftly, and they deceived the eyes of the people. ﴿And they said: By the might of Fir'awn, indeed we are the victors.﴾ They sought help by the might of a weak servant, helpless in every respect, except that he had become tyrannical and acquired the appearance of kingship and armies, and that splendor deceived them, and their insight did not penetrate to the reality of the matter; or it was an oath by them by the might of Fir'awn, and the thing sworn to is that they are the victors. ﴿Then Musa threw his staff, and behold, it swallowed﴾: it devoured and took ﴿what they had fabricated.﴾ So it seized all that they had thrown of ropes and staffs, because they were a lie, falsehood and fabrication, and all of that is vanity that cannot stand against the truth nor withstand it.

{46 – 48} When the sorcerers saw this great sign, they were certain by their knowledge that this was not sorcery, but a sign of God and a miracle announcing the truthfulness of Musa and the soundness of what he brought. ﴿So the sorcerers fell down prostrate﴾ to their Lord, ﴿saying: We have believed in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun.﴾ Falsehood was suppressed in that assembly, its leaders acknowledged its falsity, the truth became clear and manifest, so that the onlookers saw it with their own eyes.

{49 – 51} But Fir'awn refused, except in arrogance, misguidance, persistence in his error and obstinacy. He said to the sorcerers: ﴿You believed in him before I gave you permission?﴾ He marveled and made his people marvel at their boldness toward him and their hastiness in believing without his permission and consultation. ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you sorcery.﴾ This is so, though he is the one who gathered the sorcerers and his chiefs who advised him to gather them from their cities, and they knew that they had not met Musa or seen him before that, and that they had brought from sorcery what bewilders the observers and overwhelms them. Despite that, this saying which they themselves had recognized as false became acceptable to them. It is therefore not to be wondered at that people of such minds do not believe in the clear truth and the dazzling signs, for if Fir'awn had told them that it was contrary to its reality, they would have believed him. Then he threatened the sorcerers, saying: ﴿I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides﴾; that is, the right hand and the left foot, as is done to the corrupter on earth, ﴿and I will surely crucify you all,﴾ to disgrace and humiliate you. The sorcerers, when they found the sweetness of faith and tasted its delight, said: ﴿No harm!﴾; that is, we do not care about what you threaten us with. ﴿Indeed, to our Lord we will return. Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins﴾ of disbelief, sorcery and other things ﴿that we were the first of the believers﴾ in Musa among these soldiers. So God made them firm and gave them patience. It is possible that Fir'awn did to them what he threatened, by his authority and power at that time; and it is possible that God prevented him from them.

{52} Then Fir'awn and his people remained persistent in their disbelief. Musa came to them with clear signs, and whenever a sign came to them and affected them to the utmost, they promised Musa and covenanted with him that if God removed it from them, they would surely believe in him and surely send the Children of Israel with him. God would remove it, and then they would break their word. When Musa despaired of their belief, the word of punishment was due against them, and it was time for God to rescue the Children of Israel from their captivity and establish them in the land, He inspired Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾; that is, leave with the Children of Israel at the beginning of the night, so that they may proceed and go slowly in their departure. ﴿Indeed, you will be pursued﴾; that is, Fir'awn and his soldiers will follow you. It happened as He had informed: when they awoke, behold, the Children of Israel had all set out with Musa.

{53 – 56} ﴿So Fir'awn sent into the cities gatherers﴾ who gather people, to fall upon the Children of Israel, and he said, encouraging his people: ﴿Indeed, these are a small troop, few in number. And indeed, they are enraging us,﴾ so we intend to vent our rage upon these slaves who have fled from us. ﴿And indeed, we are a vigilant host﴾; that is, we must be on guard against all of them, and they are enemies to all, and the interest is shared.

{57 – 59} So Fir'awn and his soldiers went out in a great army and general mobilization, none remaining behind except those with excuses whom incapacity prevented. God the Exalted said: ﴿So We expelled them from gardens and springs,﴾ that is, the gardens of Egypt, its excellent orchards, its flowing springs, and crops that filled their lands and populated their cities and countryside with them; ﴿and noble dwellings,﴾ which delight the observers and amaze the contemplators. They enjoyed it for a long age, and they spent a long life in its pleasures and desires, in disbelief, obstinacy, arrogance over the servants, and great bewilderment. ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them,﴾ that is, these gardens, springs, crops and noble dwelling, ﴿the Children of Israel,﴾ whom they had previously made their slaves and subjugated to their hard labor. So glory be to Him who gives sovereignty to whom He wills, strips it from whom He wills, exalts whom He wills by obedience to Him, and humbles whom He wills by disobedience to Him.

{60 – 62} ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾; that is, the people of Fir'awn followed the people of Musa at the time of sunrise, driving behind them in anger and rage, capable. ﴿Then when the two companies saw each other﴾; that is, each saw the other. ﴿The companions of Musa said﴾ complaining to Musa and grieved: ﴿Indeed, we are about to be overtaken.﴾ Musa said, making them firm and informing them of the true promise of his Lord: ﴿No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me﴾ to what contains my deliverance and yours.

{63–68} {So We revealed to Moses: "Strike the sea with your staff."} So he struck it, {and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain}; that is, like a huge mountain. Moses and his people entered [the path]. {And We brought the others near to that place}; that is, Pharaoh [and] his people. We drew them near and led them into that same path which Moses and his people had taken. {And We delivered Moses and all who were with him}: they completed the crossing, coming out, and not one of them was left behind. {Then We drowned the others}: not one of them was left behind from drowning. {Indeed in that is a sign}: a great sign confirming the truth of what Moses, peace be upon him, brought and the falsehood of what Pharaoh and his people were upon. {Yet most of them were not believers}: despite these signs that call for faith, because of the corruption of your hearts. {And indeed your Lord is the Exalted in Might, the Most Merciful}: by His might He destroyed the disbelieving deniers, and by His mercy He saved Moses and all who were with him.

{69 – 71} That is: recite, O Muhammad, to the people the account of Ibrahim the Khalil (the Friend) and his magnificent report in this particular situation. Otherwise, he has many accounts. But among the most wondrous and most excellent of his accounts is this one, which contains his prophethood, his call to his people, his debate with them, and [its refutation of] what they were upon. For this reason he restricted it with a time clause, saying: ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"﴾ They said, boasting of their worship: ﴿"We worship idols, and we remain devoted to them."﴾ That is: we continue to worship them for much of our time.

{72 – 74} Ibrahim said to them, showing that they do not deserve to be worshipped: ﴿"Do they hear you when you call (on them)?"﴾, so that they respond to your supplication, relieve your distress, and remove from you every harm. ﴿"Or do they benefit you, or do they harm?"﴾ They acknowledged that none of this exists in them: they do not hear supplication, they do not benefit, and they do not harm. For this reason, when he broke them and said: ﴿"Rather, the biggest of them did this. So ask them, if they can speak,"﴾ they said to him: ﴿"You certainly know that these do not speak."﴾ That is: this is a matter established about their condition, admitting no doubt or uncertainty. Then they resorted to imitating their misguided forefathers, saying: ﴿"Rather, we found our fathers doing so."﴾ That is: we followed them in this, took their path, and preserved their customs.

{75 – 82} Ibrahim said to them: You and your fathers are all adversaries in [this] matter, and the address is to all of you alike: ﴿"Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers? Indeed, they are an enemy to me, except the Lord of the worlds, who created me and it is He who guides me, who feeds me and gives me drink, and when I am ill, it is He who cures me, who causes me to die and then gives me life, and who I hope will forgive my sin on the Day of Recompense."﴾ That is: He alone is the one who has the blessing of creation and the blessing of guidance to religious and worldly welfare. Then he specified some of the essential necessities, saying what he said. This is the One who is singled out for all of this, so He alone must be singled out for worship and obedience, and these idols that neither create nor guide, neither fall ill nor cure, neither feed nor give drink, neither cause death nor give life, and neither benefit their worshippers by relieving distress nor by forgiving sins, must be abandoned. This is a decisive proof and a dazzling argument that you and your fathers cannot oppose, which shows your shared misguidance and your abandonment of the path of guidance and rectitude. God Most High said: ﴿"His people argued with him. He said: 'Do you argue with me about God, when He has guided me?'"﴾ and the verses that follow.

{83 – 84} Then the prophet (peace be upon him) supplicated his Lord, saying: ﴿"My Lord, grant me wisdom"﴾; that is, abundant knowledge by which I may know the rulings, the lawful and the unlawful, and by which I may judge among people. ﴿"And join me with the righteous,"﴾ from among his brothers, the prophets and messengers. ﴿"And grant me a tongue of truth among the later generations."﴾ That is: grant me a truthful, continuous praise until the end of time. God answered his supplication, granting him knowledge and wisdom, by which he became among the most excellent of messengers, joined him with his messenger brothers, and made him beloved, accepted, honored, and praised by all religious communities at all times. God Most High said: ﴿"And We left for him among the later generations: Peace be upon Ibrahim. Thus do We reward the good-doers. Indeed, he was among Our believing servants."﴾

{85} ﴿"And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss,"﴾ that is: among the people of the Garden that God bequeaths to them. God answered his supplication and raised his rank in the Gardens of Bliss.

{86} ﴿"And forgive my father, for he was among the misguided."﴾ This supplication was due to the promise he had made to his father when he said: ﴿"I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He has been gracious to me."﴾ God Most High said: ﴿"Ibrahim's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disowned him. Indeed, Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing."﴾

{87 – 89} ﴿"And do not disgrace me on the Day they are resurrected,"﴾ that is: by rebuke for some sins, punishment for them, and exposure. Rather, make me happy on that day when neither wealth nor children will benefit, ﴿"except one who comes to God with a sound heart."﴾ This is the one who will benefit before You, the one who is saved from punishment and deserves abundant reward. The sound heart means: one who is free from polytheism (shirk) and doubt, from love of evil, and from persistence in innovation (bid'ah) and sins. Its soundness from what has been mentioned entails being characterized by their opposites: sincerity, knowledge, certainty, love of good, and making it beautiful in the heart; and that his will and love follow the love of God, and his desire follows what has come from God.

{90 – 95} Then He mentioned some of the characteristics of that great day and what it contains of reward and punishment, saying: ﴿"And the Garden is brought near to the righteous,"﴾ that is: made close to those who are God-fearing (muttaqun), who obey His commands, avoid His prohibitions, and guard against His wrath and punishment. ﴿"And the Hellfire is made manifest to the deviators,"﴾ that is: it is displayed and prepared with all of its punishment, for those who rush into the disobedience of God, dare to violate His sanctities, deny His messengers, and reject the truth they brought. ﴿"And it will be said to them: Where is what you used to worship besides God? Can they help you, or can they help themselves?"﴾ That is: none of that exists, their lies and disgrace become apparent, their loss and humiliation are exposed, their regret is evident, and their efforts are lost. ﴿"So they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators,"﴾ that is: those who were worshipped are cast into the Fire, and the deviators are those who worshipped them. ﴿"And the soldiers of Iblis, all of them,"﴾ from humans and jinn, who incited them to sins with incitement, and who dominated them because of their polytheism and lack of faith, so they became his callers and those who strive for his pleasure. Among them are those who call to his obedience, those who respond to them, and those who imitate them in their polytheism.

{96 – 104} ﴿"They will say"﴾; that is, the deviating soldiers of Iblis, speaking to their idols that they had worshipped: ﴿"By God, we were indeed in clear error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds."﴾ That is: in worship, love, fear, and hope, and we called upon you as we called upon Him. Then their error became clear to them, and they acknowledged God's justice in their punishment, and that it was in its proper place. They did not equate them with the Lord of the worlds except in worship, not in creation, as evidenced by their saying ﴿"the Lord of the worlds,"﴾ which shows that they affirmed that God is Lord of all the worlds, among which are their idols. ﴿"And none misled us except the criminals,"﴾ who are the leaders who call to the Fire. ﴿"So we have no intercessors,"﴾ who might intercede for us to rescue us from His punishment, ﴿"nor a close friend."﴾ That is: a dear friend who would benefit us with the least benefit, as is customary in this world. {105–110} He, exalted is He, mentions the denial of the people of Noah toward their messenger Noah, what he replied to them and what they replied to him, and the outcome for all of them. He says: {The people of Noah denied the messengers}: He gathered them, because denying Noah is like denying all the messengers, since they all agreed upon one call and one message; so denying one of them is like denying everything brought from the truth. They denied him {when their brother Noah said to them}: by lineage {Noah}. Allah only sent the messengers from among the lineage of those to whom they were sent, so that they would not recoil from submitting to them, and because they know his reality and so have no need to search for him. He addressed them with the gentlest address, as is the way of the messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them: {Will you not fear Allah}, the Exalted, so that you abandon what you persist in of worshipping idols and make worship sincerely for Allah alone. {Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger}: his being a messenger to them specifically obliges them to receive what he was sent with, to believe in it, and to thank Allah, the Exalted, for singling them out with this noble messenger. His being trustworthy requires that he not speak about Allah (falsely), nor add to or subtract from His revelation. This obliges them to affirm his report and obey his command. {So fear Allah and obey me}: in what he commands you and forbids you; for this is what follows from his being a trustworthy messenger to them. Therefore He ordered it with the particle fa' (so), which indicates causation: he mentioned the obligating cause, then mentioned the absence of an impediment, saying: {And I do not ask you for any wage for it}: so that you would bear a heavy burden of debt. {My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds}: I hope by that for nearness to Him and abundant reward; as for you, my wish and the ultimate aim of my desire from you is to advise you and that you follow the straight path. {So fear Allah and obey me}: he, peace be upon him, repeated this because of his repeated calling of his people and his long stay in that; as Allah, the Exalted, said: {So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years} and {He said: My Lord, I have called my people night and day, but my calling has only increased them in flight…} and the verses.

{111} So they said, in rejection of his call and in opposition to him with what is not fit for opposition: {Shall we believe you while the lowest (al-arhalun) follow you?}; that is: how can we follow you when we see your followers only as the lowest, most abject and base of people. By this is known their arrogance toward the truth and their ignorance of realities. For if their aim had been the truth, they would have said—if they had doubt and uncertainty about his call—"Show us the soundness of what you have brought by the means that lead to it!" And if they had reflected with due reflection, they would have known that his followers are the most exalted, the best of creation, people of sound intellects and virtuous character, and that the lowest is one who has been deprived of the distinctive quality of his intellect, so that he approves the worship of stones, is content to prostrate to them and call upon them, and refuses to submit to the call of the perfect messengers. When one of the two disputants speaks false words, the corruption of what he holds is known immediately, regardless of the validity of his opponent's claim. He addressed them with the gentlest address, as is the way of the messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them: {Will you not fear Allah}, the Exalted, so that you abandon what you persist in of worshipping idols and make worship sincerely for Allah alone. {Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger}: his being a messenger to them specifically obliges them to receive what he was sent with, to believe in it, and to thank Allah, the Exalted, for singling them out with this noble messenger. His being trustworthy requires that he not speak about Allah (falsely), nor add to or subtract from His revelation. This obliges them to affirm his report and obey his command. {So fear Allah and obey me}: in what he commands you and forbids you; for this is what follows from his being a trustworthy messenger to them. Therefore He ordered it with the particle fa' (so), which indicates causation: he mentioned the obligating cause, then mentioned the absence of an impediment, saying: {And I do not ask you for any wage for it}: so that you would bear a heavy burden of debt. {My wage is only from the Lord of the worlds}: I hope by that for nearness to Him and abundant reward; as for you, my wish and the ultimate aim of my desire from you is to advise you and that you follow the straight path. {So fear Allah and obey me}: he, peace be upon him, repeated this because of his repeated calling of his people and his long stay in that; as Allah, the Exalted, said: {So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years} and {He said: My Lord, I have called my people night and day, but my calling has only increased them in flight…} and the verses.

{111} So they said, in rejection of his call and in opposition to him with what is not fit for opposition: {Shall we believe you while the lowest (al-arhalun) follow you?}; that is: how can we follow you when we see your followers only as the lowest, most abject and base of people. By this is known their arrogance toward the truth and their ignorance of realities. For if their aim had been the truth, they would have said—if they had doubt and uncertainty about his call—"Show us the soundness of what you have brought by the means that lead to it!" And if they had reflected with due reflection, they would have known that his followers are the most exalted, the best of creation, people of sound intellects and virtuous character, and that the lowest is one who has been deprived of the distinctive quality of his intellect, so that he approves the worship of stones, is content to prostrate to them and call upon them, and refuses to submit to the call of the perfect messengers. When one of the two disputants speaks false words, the corruption of what he holds is known immediately, regardless of the validity of his opponent's claim. So when we are told that the people of Noah, in rejecting his call, said: {Shall we believe you while the lowest follow you?}, and built on this principle, whose corruption everyone knows, the rejection of his call, we know that they are astray and mistaken, even if we had not witnessed from Noah's signs and his great call what conveys certainty and conviction of his truthfulness and the soundness of what he brought.

{112–115} Noah, peace be upon him, said: {And what is my knowledge of what they used to do? Their reckoning is only upon my Lord, if you could perceive}; that is: their deeds and their reckoning are upon Allah; my duty is only to convey. As for you, leave them aside; if what I have brought you is the truth, then submit to it, and each has his own deed. {And I am not one to drive away the believers}: it seems they—may Allah disfigure them—asked him to drive them away from him out of arrogance and tyranny, so that they would believe; so he said: {And I am not one to drive away the believers}, for they do not deserve to be driven away and humiliated, but deserve honor in word and deed; as Allah, the Exalted, said: {And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say: Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy}. {I am only a clear warner}; that is: I am only a warner and a conveyer from Allah, striving sincerely for the servants, and I have no part in the affair; indeed the affair belongs only to Allah.

{116} Noah, peace and blessings be upon him, persisted in calling them night and day, secretly and openly, but they increased only in aversion. {They said: If you do not desist, O Noah}: from your calling us to Allah alone; {you will surely be among the stoned}; that is: we will surely kill you in the worst manner, by pelting with stones, as a dog is killed. Woe to them! How evil is this response! They repay the sincere, trustworthy adviser, who is more compassionate toward them than they are toward themselves, with the worst of responses.

{117–118} Indeed, when their wrongdoing reached its limit and their disbelief intensified, their prophet invoked against them a supplication that encompassed them, saying: {My Lord, leave not upon the earth any of the disbelievers a dwelling-dweller…} and the verses. Here he said: {My Lord, indeed my people have denied me, so decide between me and them a decision}; that is: destroy the transgressor among us, and he knew that they were the rebellious wrongdoers. Therefore he said: {And save me and those with me of the believers}.

{119–122} {Then We saved him and those with him in the laden ship}; that is: the ship {laden} with creatures and animals. {Then We drowned the rest afterward}; that is: after Noah and those believers with him, {the rest}; that is: all of his people. {Indeed in that}; that is: the salvation of Noah and his followers and the destruction of those who denied him {is a sign}: indicating the truthfulness of Our messengers, the soundness of what they brought, and the falsehood of what their enemies, the deniers of them, hold. {And indeed your Lord is the Almighty}: who by His might subdued His enemies and drowned them by the flood. {The Merciful}: toward His allies; in that He saved Noah and those with him of the believers.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 26, verse 123–140:

{123 – 127} That is: the tribe called ʿAd denied their messenger Hud, and their denial of him is a denial of all messengers, since the message is one. {When their brother Hud said to them}: in lineage, {"Will you not fear God?"}: gently and with good speech, meaning: will you not be wary of God, so that you abandon polytheism and the worship of other than Him? {"Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger"}; that is: God has sent me to you out of mercy for you and care for you, and I am trustworthy; you know this about me. He based on this his saying: {"So fear God and obey me"}; that is: render to God the right that is due to Him, which is taqwa (God-consciousness), and render to me my right by obeying me in what I command you and forbid you. This necessitates that you follow me and obey me, and there is no obstacle preventing you from faith. I do not ask you for a wage for my conveying to you and advising you, so that you would find this burden heavy. {"My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds"}: who nurtured them with His blessings and poured upon them His bounty and generosity, especially what He nurtured His friends and prophets with.

{128 – 135} {"Do you build on every high place"}; that is: a landmark between the mountains {"a sign"}; that is: a monument {"which you make in vain"}; that is: you do this in vain, for no benefit that returns to the good of your religion or your worldly affairs, {"and you take for yourselves fortresses"}; that is: cisterns and water reservoirs, {"that perhaps you may abide forever"}: while in fact there is no way to eternity for anyone. {"And when you strike, you strike as tyrants"}: against creatures, by killing, beating and seizing wealth. God had given them great strength, and it was obligatory upon them to use their strength in obedience to God. But they boasted, grew arrogant, and said: "Who is mightier than us in strength?" They used their strength in disobedience to God, in vanity and foolishness. Therefore their prophet forbade them from this. {"So fear God"}: and abandon your polytheism and your insolence {"and obey me"}: since you know that I am the trustworthy and sincere messenger of God to you. {"And fear He who has provided you"}; that is: who has given you {"with what you know"}; that is: He provided you with what is not unknown nor denied of livestock, {"provided you with livestock"}: camels, cattle and sheep, {"and sons"}; that is: and abundance of offspring; He increased your wealth and increased your children, especially the males, the better of the two kinds. This is a reminder of blessings. Then he reminded them of the descent of God's punishment, saying: {"Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day"}; that is: out of my compassion for you and my kindness toward you, I fear that a great punishment will descend upon you. When it descends it cannot be averted, if you persist in your disbelief and your transgression.

{136 – 138} They said, opposing the truth and denying their prophet: {"It is all the same to us whether you admonish or are not among the admonishers"}; that is: all is equal! This is the utmost obstinacy. For a people whose condition has reached the point where God's admonitions, which would melt hard, solid mountains and split the hearts of people of understanding, are to them the same whether present or absent, is a people whose wrongdoing has ended, whose wretchedness has intensified, and for whom hope of their guidance has been cut off. Therefore they said: {"This is nothing but the custom of the former peoples"}; that is: these conditions, blessings and the like are the custom of the ancients: sometimes they become wealthy, sometimes they become poor, and these are the states of time, since these are trials and gifts from God and tests for His servants. {"And we are not going to be punished"}: this is a denial of resurrection on their part, or a condescension toward their prophet and mockery of him: that even supposing we are resurrected, just as blessings have been poured upon us in this world, so they will continue to flow upon us when we are raised.

{139 – 140} {So they denied him}; that is: denial became their nature and character, with nothing to restrain them from it. {So We destroyed them}: {with a furious, violent wind. He subjected it against them for seven nights and eight days in succession, so you would see the people in it fallen down as though they were trunks of hollow palm trees.} {Indeed in that is a sign}: of the truthfulness of our prophet Hud, peace be upon him, the soundness of what he brought, and the falsehood of what his people held of polytheism and tyranny. {And most of them were not believers}: despite the presence of signs that call for faith. {And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty}: who destroyed the people of Hud by His might despite their strength and their violence. {the Merciful}: toward His prophet Hud, in that He saved him and those who were with him among the believers.

This is despite the fact that merely considering his condition and what he called to is one of the greatest clear signs of the truth of what he brought and of his sincerity. They denied Salih (peace be upon him), who came with tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness), which the messengers had all called to, so their denial of him was a denial of all of them. {When their brother Salih said to them}: in lineage, gently and kindly: {Will you not fear God}: and abandon shirk (associating partners with God) and sins? {Indeed, I am a messenger to you}: from God, your Lord, whom He sent to you out of kindness and mercy to you. So receive His mercy with acceptance, and meet it with submission. {Trustworthy}: you know this about me, and that obliges you to believe in me and in what I have brought, {and I do not ask you for any reward}: so that you would say, "What prevents us from following you is that you want to take our wealth." {My reward is only from the Lord of the worlds}; that is, I seek reward only from Him.

{145–152} {Will you be left in what is here, secure? Among gardens and springs, and crops and palm trees with fine clustered fruit}; that is, abundant clusters. That is: do you think you will be left in these bounties and blessings, idle, enjoying yourselves and taking pleasure as cattle do, and left without being commanded or forbidden, while you use these blessings to disobey God? {And you hew out of the mountains houses with skill}; that is, your skill and craftsmanship have reached the point that you have made houses out of the hard, solid mountains. {So fear God and obey me. And do not obey the command of the extravagant}: those who exceed the limit, {who spread corruption in the land and do not reform}; that is, those whose description and habit is spreading corruption in the land by committing sins and calling to them, a corruption with no reform in it, and this is the most harmful kind, because it is pure evil. It seems that there were people among them who were ready to oppose their prophet, promoting the path of error, so Salih forbade them from being deceived by them. Perhaps these are the ones of whom God said: {And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform}.

{153–154} This prohibition and admonition did not benefit them at all, so they said to Salih: {You are only one of the bewitched}; that is, you have been bewitched, so you are raving about what has no meaning, {and you are only a human like us}; so what virtue do you have over us that you should call us to follow you? {Then bring a sign, if you are of the truthful}. This is despite the fact that merely considering his condition and what he called to is one of the greatest clear signs of the truth of what he brought and of his sincerity. But out of their hardness they asked for signs of demand, which generally do not benefit those who seek them, because their seeking is based on obstinacy rather than on seeking guidance.

{155–156} Salih said: {This is a she-camel}: emerging from a hard, smooth rock (in this we follow many of the exegetes, and there is no objection to that), which you see and witness, all of you. {She has a drink, and you have a drink on a known day}; that is, she drinks the water of the well one day, and you drink her milk; then on the next day she leaves you, and you drink the water of the well. {And do not touch her with harm}: by hamstringing or otherwise; {or the punishment of a tremendous day will seize you}.

{157–159} So she came forth and remained among them in that state, but they did not believe and persisted in their rebellion. {They hamstrung her, and so they became regretful. The punishment seized them}: it was a cry that descended upon them, destroying them all. {Indeed, in that is a sign}: of the truth of what Our messengers brought and the falsehood of the words of their opponents. {Yet most of them were not believers. And indeed, your Lord is the Mighty, the Merciful}.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 26, verses 176–191:**

{176–180} "The People of the Thicket" (Ashab al-Aykah), i.e., the gardens with densely intertwined trees, and they are the people of Madyan. They denied their prophet Shu'ayb, who came with what the messengers came with. ﴿When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not be mindful of God?"﴾: that you would abandon what angers and provokes Him of disbelief and sins. ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.﴾: it follows from this that you should fear God and obey me.

{181–184} And they, along with their polytheism, would cheat in measures and weights; therefore he said to them: ﴿Give full measure﴾, i.e., complete it and perfect it. ﴿And do not be among the causers of loss﴾: those who diminish people's wealth and take it away by cheating in the measure and the scale. ﴿And weigh with an even balance﴾, i.e., with a just scale that does not tilt. ﴿And fear the One who created you and the former generations﴾, i.e., the earlier creation. Just as He alone created you and those before you, without any partner in that, so single Him out in worship and monotheism; and just as He has blessed you with existence and provided you with favors, so respond to Him with gratitude.

{185–187} They said to him, denying him and rejecting his words: ﴿You are only one of the bewitched﴾: you are raving and speaking the words of one under magic, whose only consequence is that he is not held accountable for them. ﴿And you are not but a human like us﴾: there is no virtue in you by which you have distinguished yourself over us, so that you would call us to follow you. This is like the saying of those before them and those after them, of those who opposed the messengers with this doubt, which they never ceased to put forward, to assault with, and to agree upon, because of their agreement in disbelief and the similarity of their hearts. The messengers answered it with their words: ﴿We are not but humans like you, but God bestows His favor upon whom He wills of His servants.﴾ ﴿And indeed, we think you are among the liars.﴾: this is audacity, injustice, and a false statement on their part, while they had concealed the opposite of it; for no messenger has ever confronted his people, called them, argued with them, and they argued with him, except that God has manifested through his hands signs by which they become certain of his truthfulness and trustworthiness. This is especially so for Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, who is called the orator of the prophets (Khatib al-Anbiya') because of his excellent way of addressing his people and disputing with them in the best manner; for his people were certain of his truthfulness and that what he brought was true, but their claim that they suspected him of lying was a lie on their part. ﴿So cause fragments of the sky to fall upon us﴾, i.e., a piece of punishment that will destroy us, ﴿if you are of the truthful.﴾ Like the saying of their brethren: ﴿And when they said, "O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ Or they sought some of the signs of demand (ayat al-iqtira') whose fulfillment of what the one who asked for them seeks is not binding.

{188} ﴿Shu'ayb said﴾, peace be upon him: ﴿My Lord is most knowing of what you do﴾, i.e., the descent of punishment and the occurrence of the signs of demand: I am not the one who brings them or sends them down upon you; my duty is only to convey to you and advise you, and I have done so. The one who brings them is my Lord, who knows your deeds and conditions, who will recompense and hold you accountable.

{189–191} ﴿So they denied him﴾, i.e., denial became their attribute and disbelief their constant habit, such that the signs no longer benefited them, and there was no recourse for them except the descent of punishment. ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them﴾: a cloud shaded them, so they gathered beneath it, delighting in its shade, which was not a cooling shade; then it burned them with punishment, so they remained beneath it lifeless, departing from their homes and descending into the abode of misery and punishment. ﴿Indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous Day.﴾: they will have no return to the world to resume their deeds, and the punishment will not be lightened for them for a moment, nor will they be reprieved. ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾: indicating the truthfulness of Shu'ayb, the correctness of what he called to, and the falsehood of his people's rejection of him. ﴿But most of them were not believers﴾: despite seeing the signs, because there is no purity in them and no good in them; ﴿And most of mankind, even if you were eager, would not be believers.﴾ ﴿And indeed, your Lord is the Exalted in Might﴾: who, by His power, is beyond the perception of anyone, and subdues every creature. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾: whose attribute is mercy, and from whose effects are all goods in this world and the Hereafter, from the time God brought the world into existence to an endless end. From His might is that He destroyed His enemies when they denied His messengers, and from His mercy is that He saved His allies and those among the believers who followed them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 26, verses 192–203:

{192} When He had mentioned the stories of the prophets with their peoples, how they called them and were answered in return, and how Allah destroyed their enemies and the final outcome became theirs, He mentioned this noble Messenger and the great chosen Prophet, and the Book he brought, which contains guidance for people of understanding. So He said: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾. The One who sent it down is the Creator of the earth and the heavens, the Sustainer of all the worlds, the upper and the lower. Just as He nurtures them by guiding them to the benefits of their worldly life and their bodies, He also nurtures them by guiding them to the benefits of their religion and their Hereafter. Among the greatest of what He has nurtured them with is the sending down of this noble Book, which includes much good and abundant righteousness, and which contains guidance to the benefits of both abodes and to noble character that is not found in any other. [And] in His saying ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾ there is a glorification of it and a strong emphasis on it, by the fact that it was sent down from Allah and not from anyone else, with its benefit and your guidance intended.

{193–195} ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾: this is Jibril (peace be upon him), who is the best and strongest of the angels, the Trustworthy, who is secure from adding to it or subtracting from it. ﴿Upon your heart﴾: O Muhammad, ﴿that you may be of the warners﴾: you guide by it to the path of rectitude and warn by it against the path of error. ﴿In clear Arabic language﴾: and it is the best of tongues, in the language of those to whom he was sent and whose call he originally undertook, the clear and evident tongue.
Reflect on how these excellent virtues have come together in this noble Book: it is the best of books, brought down by the best of angels, upon the best of creation, upon the best part of him, which is his heart, to the best of nations raised up for mankind, in the best, most eloquent and most comprehensive of tongues, which is the clear Arabic language.

{196} ﴿And indeed, it is in the scriptures of the former peoples﴾; that is, the books of the former peoples gave glad tidings of it and confirmed it. And when it was sent down in accordance with what they had reported, it confirmed them; rather, it came with the truth and confirmed the messengers.

{197} ﴿Is it not a sign for them﴾: of its soundness and that it is from Allah, ﴿that it is known by the scholars of the Children of Israel﴾: those to whom knowledge has come, who have become the most knowledgeable of people, and who are the people of specialization. For everything in which confusion arises is referred back to the people of experience and insight, so their word becomes a proof over others. Just as the sorcerers who had mastered the science of magic recognized the truth of Musa's miracle and that it was not sorcery, so the words of the ignorant after this carry no weight.

{198–199} ﴿And if We had sent it down upon some of the non-Arabs﴾: who do not understand their language and are unable to express it to them as they should. ﴿And he recited it to them, they would not have been believers in it﴾: they would say, "We do not understand what he says, and we do not know what he calls us to!" So let them praise their Lord that it came to them in the tongue of the most eloquent of creation and the most capable of expressing intended meanings in clear and most sincere words, and let them hasten to affirm it and receive it with submission and acceptance.

{200–203} But their denial of it, without any doubt, is nothing but pure disbelief and obstinacy, a matter inherited by the denying nations. Therefore He said: ﴿Thus We have caused it to enter into the hearts of the criminals﴾; that is, We inserted denial and threaded it into the hearts of the people of sin, just as a thread enters a needle, so that it soaked into them and became a attribute of theirs. This is due to their wrongdoing and crime. Therefore ﴿they will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment﴾ for their denial, ﴿so it will come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾; that is, it will come upon them at a moment of heedlessness, without their sensing or anticipating its descent, so that it will be more severe in its punishment and retribution against them. ﴿And they will say﴾ at that time: ﴿Will we be reprieved?﴾; that is, they will seek to be given respite and delay, while the time has already passed and the punishment has descended upon them, which will not be lifted from them nor lightened for an hour.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 26, verse 208–212:

{208 – 209} He, exalted is He, informs of the perfection of His justice in destroying those who deny (the truth), and that He never inflicts destruction and punishment upon a town except after He has established the proof against them and sent to them warners with clear signs. They call them to guidance and forbid them from ruin, and remind them of the signs of Allah and alert them to His days (of favour and vengeance) in His blessings and His retributions. {Reminder} for them and the establishment of proof against them. {And We were never unjust} by destroying the towns before We warn them, and seizing them while they are heedless of the warnings, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ and ﴿messengers bearing good news and warning, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾.

{210 – 212} When He, exalted is He, had made clear the perfection of the Qur'an and its majesty, He declared it free from every attribute of deficiency and protected it, at the time of its revelation and after its revelation, from the devils of the jinn and of mankind. So He said: ﴿And the devils did not bring it down. It is not befitting for them, nor are they able to (do so).﴾ That is, it is not suitable for their state and does not fit them. ﴿Indeed, they are removed from hearing it.﴾ They have been kept far from it, and shooting stars have been prepared to guard it. It was brought down by Jibril, the strongest of the angels, whom no devil can approach or come near to its precinct. This is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We are its guardian.﴾

{213} God, exalted is He, forbids His Messenger, and his community as an example to follow in this, from calling upon anyone other than God, from all created beings. This is because it entails everlasting punishment and eternal retribution, since it is shirk (association of partners with God). Whoever associates partners with God, God has forbidden him Paradise, and his abode is the Fire. The prohibition of a thing is a command to its opposite. Thus, the prohibition of shirk is a command to devote worship sincerely to God alone, with no partner, in love, fear, hope, humility, and turning to Him in repentance at all times.

{214} When He commanded him with what perfects his own self, He commanded him to perfect others, saying: {And warn your nearest kindred}: those who are closest of people to you, and most deserving of your religious and worldly kindness. This does not contradict His command to warn all people, just as when a person is commanded with general kindness and then told: "Be kind to your relatives." This particular mention indicates emphasis and added encouragement. The Messenger (ﷺ) complied with this divine command: he summoned all the clans of Quraysh, addressing them generally and specifically, reminding and admonishing them, and he left nothing within his capacity of counsel and guidance that he did not do. Whoever was guided was guided, and whoever turned away turned away.

{215} {And lower your wing to the believers who follow you}: by gentleness of demeanour, kindness of address to them, affection and endearment toward them, good character, and complete kindness to them. The Messenger (ﷺ) did this, as God, exalted is He, said: {It is by a mercy from God that you were gentle with them. And had you been rude and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter} [Ali 'Imran 3:159]. Such were the character traits of the Messenger (ﷺ), the most perfect of characters, through which great benefits are obtained and harms repelled, as is evident. Is it fitting for a believer in God and His Messenger, who claims to follow and emulate him, to be a burden upon the Muslims, harsh of character, stiff-necked toward them, hard-hearted, coarse and vile in speech, and if he sees from them disobedience or bad manners, he shuns them, detests them, and hates them, having no gentleness, no courtesy, and no success? Such treatment has produced corruptions and the disruption of benefits to the extent that it has, and yet you find him holding in contempt those who possess the qualities of the noble Messenger, and accusing them of hypocrisy and flattery, while he exalts himself, lifts himself up, and is pleased with his own deeds?! Is this anything but his ignorance and Satan's embellishment and deception of him?!

{216} For this reason God said to His Messenger: {But if they disobey you}: in some matter; then do not disassociate yourself from them, nor abandon dealing with them with lowering the wing and gentleness of manner. Rather, disassociate yourself from their deed: admonish them concerning it, advise them, and exert your ability in turning them away from it and in their repentance from it. This qualification is a safeguard against the one who imagines that His saying {And lower your wing to the believers} requires approval of everything that comes from them so long as they are believers; so this qualification repels that notion. And God knows best.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 26, verses 217–220:

{217} The greatest aid to a servant in carrying out what he has been commanded is to rely upon his Lord and to seek help from his Master in being granted success to carry out what is commanded. For this reason, Allah the Most High commanded reliance upon Him, saying: ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful.﴾ Tawakkul (reliance upon God) is the heart's dependence upon Allah the Most High in bringing about benefits and warding off harms, together with trust in Him and good opinion of Him that what is sought will be attained. For He is Mighty and Merciful: by His might He is able to bring good to His servant and to ward off evil from him, and by His mercy toward him He does so.

{218–220} Then He alerted him to seeking help by calling to mind the nearness of Allah and dwelling in the station of ihsan (excellence in worship), saying: ﴿Who sees you when you stand [in prayer], and your movements among those who prostrate.﴾ That is: He sees you in this great act of worship, which is the salah (prayer), at the time of your standing and your movements, bowing and prostrating. He singled it out for mention because of its excellence and nobility, and because whoever calls to mind in it the nearness of his Lord becomes humble, submissive, and perfects it; and by perfecting it, the rest of his deeds are perfected, and he seeks help through it in all his affairs. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾: of all voices, in their variety, their diversity, and their differences. ﴿the All-Knowing﴾: who encompasses the outward and the inward, the unseen and the witnessed. Thus the servant's calling to mind that Allah sees him in all his states, hears everything he utters, and knows what his heart harbours of concern, resolve, and intentions, is something that helps him attain the station of ihsan.

This is a reply to those among the deniers of the Messenger who said that a devil descends upon Muhammad, and to those who said that he is a poet.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 26, verse 221–227:

{221 – 223} He said: {Shall I inform you}; that is, I will tell you the true news, about which there is no doubt and no uncertainty, of the one upon whom the devils descend; that is, according to the description of the persons upon whom the devils descend. {They descend upon every lying sinner}; that is, every liar who speaks much falsehood and deceit with untruth, {sinner}: in his deeds, abounding in sins. This is the one upon whom the devils descend, and whose condition corresponds to their condition. {They cast} upon him {the hearing}: which they steal from the heaven, {and most of them are liars}; that is, most of what they cast to him is falsehood. He speaks one truth and lies a hundred times along with it, so truth becomes mixed with falsehood, and the truth is diminished due to its scarcity and his lack of knowledge. This is the description of the persons upon whom the devils descend, and this is the description of their revelation to him.

As for Muhammad (ﷺ), his condition is contrary to these conditions in the greatest possible contrast, for he is the truthful, trustworthy, righteous, and rightly guided, who combined righteousness of heart, truthfulness of speech, and purity of deeds from what is forbidden. The revelation that descends upon him from Allah descends guarded and protected, containing the great truth about which there is no doubt and no uncertainty. So, O people of intellect, do this and those two stand equal?! Would they be confused by anyone except a madman who does not discern or distinguish between things?!

{224 – 226} When He exonerated him from the descent of the devils upon him, He also cleared him of poetry, saying: {And the poets}; that is, shall I also inform you about the established state and description of the poets; for {those who go astray follow them}: from the path of guidance, those who turn to the path of error and perdition. They themselves are astray, and you find their followers every erring, misguided, corrupt person. {Do you not see}: their error and the severity of their misguidance, {that they wander in every valley}: of the valleys of poetry, {wandering}: sometimes in praise, sometimes in blame, sometimes in truth, sometimes in falsehood, sometimes they engage in love poetry, and at other times they mock, at times they revel, and at other times they grieve; so no settled resting place is theirs, and they do not remain steadfast in any state. {And that they say what they do not do}; that is, this is the description of the poets: that their words contradict their deeds. When you hear the poet composing tender love poetry, you say: this is the most passionate of people, while his heart is empty of that; and when you hear him praising or blaming, you say: this is truth! And it is falsehood. Sometimes he boasts of deeds he did not do, abandonments he did not abandon, generosity that never came near his threshold, and bravery by which he rises above the knights, while you find him more cowardly than every coward. This is their description. So look: does it correspond to the condition of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), the rightly guided and righteous, whom every rightly guided and guided person follows, who has remained upright upon guidance and avoided perdition, whose deeds did not contradict one another, [and whose deeds did not contradict his words]; who commands only good, forbids only evil, never informed of anything except that it was truthful, never commanded anything except that he was the first to do it, and never forbade anything except that he was the first to abandon it? So does his condition correspond to the condition of the poets, or come close to them? Or is he contrary to them in every respect? So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon this most perfect Messenger and most excellent resolute one, forever and ever, eternally, who is neither a poet, nor a sorcerer, nor a madman, and for whom nothing is fitting except every perfection.

{227} When He described the poets with what He described them with, He excepted from them those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, did righteous deeds, remembered Allah much, and defended themselves against their polytheist enemies after they had been wronged. Thus their poetry became one of their righteous deeds and fruits of their faith, because it includes praise of the people of faith, victory over the people of polytheism and disbelief, defense of the religion of Allah, clarification of beneficial knowledge, and exhortation to noble morals. So He said: {Except those who believed and did righteous deeds and remembered Allah much and defended themselves after they had been wronged. And those who did wrong will know what [sort of] return they will be returned to}: to a station and reckoning that leaves nothing small or great unaccounted for, and no right unfulfilled. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 26, verse 221–227:

{221 – 223} He said: {Shall I inform you}; that is, I will tell you the true news, about which there is no doubt and no uncertainty, of the one upon whom the devils descend; that is, according to the description of the persons upon whom the devils descend. {They descend upon every lying sinner}; that is, every liar who speaks much falsehood and deceit with untruth, {sinner}: in his deeds, abounding in sins. This is the one upon whom the devils descend, and whose condition corresponds to their condition. {They cast} upon him {the hearing}: which they steal from the heaven, {and most of them are liars}; that is, most of what they cast to him is falsehood. He speaks one truth and lies a hundred times along with it, so truth becomes mixed with falsehood, and the truth is diminished due to its scarcity and his lack of knowledge. This is the description of the persons upon whom the devils descend, and this is the description of their revelation to him.

As for Muhammad (ﷺ), his condition is contrary to these conditions in the greatest possible contrast, for he is the truthful, trustworthy, righteous, and rightly guided, who combined righteousness of heart, truthfulness of speech, and purity of deeds from what is forbidden. The revelation that descends upon him from Allah descends guarded and protected, containing the great truth about which there is no doubt and no uncertainty. So, O people of intellect, do this and those two stand equal?! Would they be confused by anyone except a madman who does not discern or distinguish between things?!

{224 – 226} When He exonerated him from the descent of the devils upon him, He also cleared him of poetry, saying: {And the poets}; that is, shall I also inform you about the established state and description of the poets; for {those who go astray follow them}: from the path of guidance, those who turn to the path of error and perdition. They themselves are astray, and you find their followers every erring, misguided, corrupt person. {Do you not see}: their error and the severity of their misguidance, {that they wander in every valley}: of the valleys of poetry, {wandering}: sometimes in praise, sometimes in blame, sometimes in truth, sometimes in falsehood, sometimes they engage in love poetry, and at other times they mock, at times they revel, and at other times they grieve; so no settled resting place is theirs, and they do not remain steadfast in any state. {And that they say what they do not do}; that is, this is the description of the poets: that their words contradict their deeds. When you hear the poet composing tender love poetry, you say: this is the most passionate of people, while his heart is empty of that; and when you hear him praising or blaming, you say: this is truth! And it is falsehood. Sometimes he boasts of deeds he did not do, abandonments he did not abandon, generosity that never came near his threshold, and bravery by which he rises above the knights, while you find him more cowardly than every coward. This is their description. So look: does it correspond to the condition of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), the rightly guided and righteous, whom every rightly guided and guided person follows, who has remained upright upon guidance and avoided perdition, whose deeds did not contradict one another, [and whose deeds did not contradict his words]; who commands only good, forbids only evil, never informed of anything except that it was truthful, never commanded anything except that he was the first to do it, and never forbade anything except that he was the first to abandon it? So does his condition correspond to the condition of the poets, or come close to them? Or is he contrary to them in every respect? So may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon this most perfect Messenger and most excellent resolute one, forever and ever, eternally, who is neither a poet, nor a sorcerer, nor a madman, and for whom nothing is fitting except every perfection.

{227} When He described the poets with what He described them with, He excepted from them those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, did righteous deeds, remembered Allah much, and defended themselves against their polytheist enemies after they had been wronged. Thus their poetry became one of their righteous deeds and fruits of their faith, because it includes praise of the people of faith, victory over the people of polytheism and disbelief, defense of the religion of Allah, clarification of beneficial knowledge, and exhortation to noble morals. So He said: {Except those who believed and did righteous deeds and remembered Allah much and defended themselves after they had been wronged. And those who did wrong will know what [sort of] return they will be returned to}: to a station and reckoning that leaves nothing small or great unaccounted for, and no right unfulfilled. And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
